examples.en: Of all these, I like sushi the most.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_が_いちばん～_A_ga_ichiban～_20250209_この中で寿司が一番好きです.mp3
examples.jp: この中で、寿司が一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Kono naka de, sushi ga ichiban suki desu.

examples.en: She can swim the fastest in the class.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_が_いちばん～_A_ga_ichiban～_20250209_彼女はクラスで一番速く泳げます.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はクラスで一番速く泳げます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kurasu de ichiban hayaku oyogemasu.

examples.en: In this town, this park is the most beautiful.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_が_いちばん～_A_ga_ichiban～_20250209_この町ではこの公園が一番きれいです.mp3

examples.romaji: Kono machi de wa, kono kouen ga ichiban kirei desu.

examples.en: Among all drinks, I like tea the most.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_が_いちばん～_A_ga_ichiban～_20250209_飲み物の中では紅茶が一番好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 飲み物の中では、紅茶が一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Nomimono no naka de wa, koucha ga ichiban suki desu.

grammars.formation: Noun + が + いちばん + Adjective/Verb
grammars.long_explanation: The A が いちばん～ grammar point is used to express a superlative degree or the highest rank. It can be translated as 'the most', 'the best', or 'the least' in English. The formation is used with various adjectives and verbs, and can also be used in comparison with other items or people.
grammars.short_explanation: Express the superlative degree; 'the most', 'the best', 'the least'.
grammars.title: A が いちばん～ (A ga ichiban～)

examples.en: It is sunny today. However, it is cold.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aけれども～BA_Keredomo_B_20250209_今日は晴れているけれども寒いです.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は晴れている。けれども、寒いです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa harete iru. Keredo mo, samui desu.

examples.en: She is noisy. But, she is interesting.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aけれども～BA_Keredomo_B_20250209_彼女はうるさいけれども面白いです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はうるさい。けれども、面白いです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa urusai. Keredo mo, omoshiroi desu.

examples.en: The movie was long. But, it wasn't boring.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aけれども～BA_Keredomo_B_20250209_その映画は長かったけれども退屈じゃなかった.mp3
examples.jp: その映画は長かった。けれども、退屈じゃなかった。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa nagakatta. Keredo mo, taikutsu janakatta.

examples.en: He is good at sports. However, he is not good at studying.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aけれども～BA_Keredomo_B_20250209_彼は運動が得意だけれども勉強は苦手だ.mp3

examples.romaji: Kare wa undou ga tokui da. Keredo mo, benkyou wa nigate da.

grammars.formation: Statement A + けれども、+ Statement B
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point A。けれども、～B。 is used to express a contrast or contradiction between statement A and statement B. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however' in English. けれども is a conjunction that links two clauses to show there is a conflicting or opposing idea between them.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express a contrast between two statements. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however'.
grammars.title: A。けれども、～B。(A. Keredomo,~ B.)

examples.en: I'm busy today. However, if I have time, let's have coffee.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aしかし～B_A_Shikashi_B_20250209_今日は忙しいしかし時間があるならコーヒーを飲もう.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は忙しい。しかし、時間があるなら、コーヒーを飲もう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa isogashii. Shikashi, jikan ga aru nara, koohii o nomou.

examples.en: The movie was interesting. But, it was too long.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aしかし～B_A_Shikashi_B_20250209_その映画は面白かったしかし長すぎました.mp3
examples.jp: その映画は面白かった。しかし、長すぎました。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa omoshirokatta. Shikashi, nagasugimashita.

examples.en: He was tired. However, he finished his homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aしかし～B_A_Shikashi_B_20250209_彼は疲れていたしかし宿題を終わらせた.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は疲れていた。しかし、宿題を終わらせた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tsukareteita. Shikashi, shukudai o owaraseta.

examples.en: The room is small. But, it is in a convenient location.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aしかし～B_A_Shikashi_B_20250209_部屋は狭いですしかし便利な場所にあります.mp3
examples.jp: 部屋は狭いです。しかし、便利な場所にあります。
examples.romaji: Heya wa semai desu. Shikashi, benri na basho ni arimasu.

grammars.formation: Sentence A + しかし + Sentence B.
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point A。しかし、～B。 is used to show contrast or contradiction between two clauses. It can be translated as 'A, but B' or 'A, however B' in English. しかし is placed between two sentences to indicate a contrast between them.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
grammars.title: A。しかし、～B。 (A. Shikashi, ~B.)

examples.en: There's no time for a movie. Well then, let's go another time.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aじゃ～BA_Ja_B_20250209_映画は時間がないじゃまた今度行こう.mp3
examples.jp: 映画は時間がない。じゃ、また今度行こう。
examples.romaji: Eiga wa jikan ga nai. Ja, mata kondo ikou.

examples.en: I'm hungry. In that case, let's go to a restaurant.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aじゃ～BA_Ja_B_20250209_お腹がすいたじゃレストランに行こう.mp3
examples.jp: お腹がすいた。じゃ、レストランに行こう。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita. Ja, resutoran ni ikou.

examples.en: The train is late. So, let's go by bus.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aじゃ～BA_Ja_B_20250209_電車が遅れたじゃバスで行こう.mp3
examples.jp: 電車が遅れた。じゃ、バスで行こう。
examples.romaji: Densha ga okureta. Ja, basu de ikou.

examples.en: This shirt is expensive. Well then, let's buy a different one.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aじゃ～BA_Ja_B_20250209_このシャツは高いじゃ別のを買おう.mp3
examples.jp: このシャツは高い。じゃ、別のを買おう。
examples.romaji: Kono shatsu wa takai. Ja, betsu no o kau.

grammars.formation: A: Sentence, B: Sentence (A and B can be any sentence type)
grammars.long_explanation: The A。じゃ、～B。grammar point is used to express a decision, suggestion, or course of action based on a given situation or information. It can be translated as 'well then', 'in that case', or 'so' in English. This grammar works with any form of sentence, whether it's a verb, noun, い-adjective, or な-adjective in both parts (A and B).
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates a decision or suggestion; 'well then', 'in that case', 'so'.
grammars.title: A。じゃ、～B。(A. Ja, ~B.)

examples.en: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go watch a movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれじゃ～BA_SorejaB_20250209_今日は休みですそれじゃ映画を観に行きましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は休みです。それじゃ、映画を観に行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi desu. Soreja, eiga wo mi ni ikimashou.

examples.en: The electricity went out. In that case, let's use candles.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれじゃ～BA_SorejaB_20250209_電気が切れたそれじゃろうそくを使いましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 電気が切れた。それじゃ、ろうそくを使いましょう。
examples.romaji: Denki ga kireta. Soreja, rousoku wo tsukaimashou.

examples.en: The restaurant is crowded. In that case, let's eat somewhere else.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれじゃ～BA_SorejaB_20250209_レストランが混んでいますそれじゃ別の場所で食べましょう.mp3
examples.jp: レストランが混んでいます。それじゃ、別の場所で食べましょう。
examples.romaji: Resutoran ga kondeimasu. Soreja, betsu no basho de tabemashou.

examples.en: It seems it will rain tomorrow. In that case, let's cancel the picnic.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれじゃ～BA_SorejaB_20250209_明日は雨が降るらしいそれじゃピクニックは中止しましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 明日は雨が降るらしい。それじゃ、ピクニックは中止しましょう。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa ame ga furu rashii. Soreja, pikunikku wa chuushi shimashou.

grammars.formation: Sentence A + 。それじゃ、 + Sentence B
grammars.long_explanation: The A。それじゃ、～B。grammar point is used to connect two sentences or ideas. It translates to 'A, so/in that case, B' in English. This expression is used when the first sentence (A) creates a situation or context and the second sentence (B) indicates the consequence or response to that situation.
grammars.short_explanation: Connect two sentences; 'A, so/in that case, B'
grammars.title: A。それじゃ、～B。(A. Soreja,~B.)

examples.en: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go see a movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれでは～BA_SoredewaB_20250209_今日は休みだそれでは映画を見に行こう.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は休みだ。それでは、映画を見に行こう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi da. Sore dewa, eiga wo mi ni ikou.

examples.jp: このパンはもう古いです。それでは、捨てましょう。
examples.romaji: Kono pan wa mou furui desu. Sore dewa, sutemashou.

examples.en: It started raining. In that case, let's play indoors.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれでは～BA_SoredewaB_20250209_雨が降ってきたそれでは室内で遊ぼう.mp3
examples.jp: 雨が降ってきた。それでは、室内で遊ぼう。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futtekita. Sore dewa, shitsunai de asobou.

examples.en: I'm hungry. So, let's go eat something.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Aそれでは～BA_SoredewaB_20250209_お腹が空いたそれでは何か食べに行きましょう.mp3
examples.jp: お腹が空いた。それでは、何か食べに行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita. Sore dewa, nani ka tabe ni ikimashou.

grammars.formation: A (Statement) + 。それでは、 + B (Follow-up action or statement)
grammars.long_explanation: The A。それでは、～B。grammar point is used to express a change in situation or transition from one action to another. It can be translated as 'then', 'in that case', or 'so' in English. The formation consists of two sentences or clauses, with それでは connecting them and reflecting a change based on the previous statement (A).
grammars.short_explanation: Express a change in situation; 'then', 'in that case', 'so'.
grammars.title: A。それでは、～B。(A. Soredewa,~B.)

examples.romaji: Kudamono dewa, ringo ga ichiban suki desu.

examples.romaji: Supōtsu dewa, sakkā ga ichiban ninki desu.

examples.romaji: Kyou no tenki dewa, ame ga furisou desu.

examples.en: As for cooking, I am best at Japanese cuisine.

examples.romaji: Ryouri dewa, washoku ga ichiban tokui desu.

grammars.formation: Noun A + では、 + Subject + Predicate B
grammars.long_explanation: The A では、～B grammar point is used to indicate a contrast or comparison between A and B. It is used to express that 'As for A, ~ B' or 'Regarding A, ~ B'. This grammar structure is often used for contrasting or comparing different subjects/topics.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates a contrast or comparison between A and B; 'As for A, ~B'.
grammars.title: A。 では、～B。 (A. Dewa, ~B)

examples.en: Yesterday was cold. But today it's warm.

examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yuumei da. Demo, totemo kenkyo desu.

grammars.formation: Clause A + でも + Clause B
grammars.long_explanation: The A。でも、～B。grammar point is used to express contrast or an unexpected continuation from statement A to statement B. It can be translated as 'A, but B' or 'A, however B' in English. The formation simply places でも at the beginning of the second sentence to show contrast with the first sentence.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express contrast between two statements; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
grammars.title: A。でも、～B。(A. Demo, ~B)

grammars.formation: Aと Bと どちら + Verb/Adjective/Noun

grammars.short_explanation: Used to ask which of two alternatives is preferred or to compare two things
grammars.title: Aと Bと どちら～ (A to B to dochira~)

examples.romaji: Nihongo to kankokugo to docchi o benkyou shitai?

grammars.formation: AとBと どっち + Verb, AかBか どっち + Verb
grammars.long_explanation: The  AとBと どっち〜 grammar point is used to ask which one to choose between two options, A and B. It can be translated as 'which', 'A or B' in English. This is often used in casual speech and can be shortened to  AかBか どっち〜.

grammars.short_explanation: Indicates that there is something unique or different about A and describes what is special about it.
grammars.title: A は B が〜 (A wa B ga〜)

examples.en: The supermarket is cheaper than the convenience store.

examples.romaji: Suupaa wa konbini yori yasui desu.

grammars.formation: A は B より + Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The A は B より grammar point is used to express a comparison between two items or subjects (A and B). It can be translated as 'A is more/less than B' in English. This structure is followed by an adjective that describes the comparison.
grammars.short_explanation: Express a comparison between A and B; 'A is more/less than B'.
grammars.title: A は B より～ (A wa B yori～)

examples.en: Hamburgers are more delicious than pizza.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_より_B_のほうが～_A_yori_B_no_hou_ga_～_20250209_ピザよりハンバーガーのほうが美味しい.mp3
examples.jp: ピザよりハンバーガーのほうが美味しい。
examples.romaji: Piza yori hanbaagaa no hou ga oishii.

examples.en: Winter is colder than summer.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_より_B_のほうが～_A_yori_B_no_hou_ga_～_20250209_夏より冬のほうが寒い.mp3
examples.jp: 夏より冬のほうが寒い。
examples.romaji: Natsu yori fuyu no hou ga samui.

examples.en: There is quieter than here.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_より_B_のほうが～_A_yori_B_no_hou_ga_～_20250209_ここよりそこのほうが静かです.mp3
examples.jp: ここよりそこのほうが静かです。
examples.romaji: Koko yori soko no hou ga shizuka desu.

examples.en: Trains are faster than cars.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_A_より_B_のほうが～_A_yori_B_no_hou_ga_～_20250209_車より電車のほうが速い.mp3
examples.jp: 車より電車のほうが速い。
examples.romaji: Kuruma yori densha no hou ga hayai.

grammars.formation: A + より + B + のほうが + Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point A より B のほうが～ is used to compare two items or situations and indicate that one is more (adjective) than the other. It can be translated as 'B is more ～ than A' in English. It is used with both い-adjectives and な-adjectives.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to compare two items; 'B is more ～ than A'.
grammars.title: A より B のほうが～ (A yori B no hou ga ～)

examples.en: He ran quickly.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_+_Verb_i-Adjective_+_ku_+_Verb_20250209_彼は速く走りました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は速く走りました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa hayaku hashirimashita.

examples.en: I enjoyed eating this dish.

examples.jp: この料理は美味しく食べました。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa oishiku tabemashita.

examples.en: She speaks kindly.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_+_Verb_i-Adjective_+_ku_+_Verb_20250209_彼女は優しく話します.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は優しく話します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yasashiku hanashimasu.

examples.en: My mother is working busily.

examples.jp: 母は忙しく仕事をしています。
examples.romaji: Haha wa isogashiku shigoto o shite imasu.

grammars.formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + く + Verb
grammars.long_explanation: The い-Adjective + く + Verb grammar point transforms an い-adjective into its adverbial form, describing how the verb is performed. In English, this often corresponds to '-ly' adverbs (e.g., 'quickly', 'slowly').
grammars.short_explanation: Used to connect an い-adjective to a verb, modifying the verb (adverbial usage).
grammars.title: い-Adjective く + Verb (i-Adjective + ku + Verb)

examples.en: I will make the room brighter.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_します_i-Adjective_ku_shimasu_20250209_部屋を明るくします.mp3
examples.jp: 部屋を明るくします。
examples.romaji: Heya o akaruku shimasu.

examples.en: I will make my friend’s mood more pleasant.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_します_i-Adjective_ku_shimasu_20250209_友達の気分を楽しくします.mp3
examples.jp: 友達の気分を楽しくします。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi no kibun o tanoshiku shimasu.

examples.en: I will make the way of doing things faster so that the work becomes easier.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_します_i-Adjective_ku_shimasu_20250209_仕事が簡単になるようにやり方を早くします.mp3
examples.jp: 仕事が簡単になるように、やり方を早くします。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga kantan ni naru you ni, yarikata o hayaku shimasu.

examples.en: I will make the food delicious.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_く_します_i-Adjective_ku_shimasu_20250209_食べ物を美味しくします.mp3
examples.jp: 食べ物を美味しくします。
examples.romaji: Tabemono o oishiku shimasu.

grammars.formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くします
grammars.long_explanation: By adding くします to an い-adjective, you express making something (or causing something to become) the quality of that adjective. In English, this often corresponds to phrases like 'make something more ADJECTIVE.'
grammars.short_explanation: Use an い-adjective to express 'to make' or 'to become'.
grammars.title: い-Adjective く します (i-Adjective ku shimasu)

examples.en: This pizza is not delicious.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective:_Negative_Polite_Form_20250209_このピザは美味しくないです.mp3
examples.jp: このピザは美味しくないです。
examples.romaji: Kono piza wa oishiku nai desu.

examples.en: This room is not spacious.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective:_Negative_Polite_Form_20250209_この部屋は広くないです.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋は広くないです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hiroku nai desu.

examples.en: His opinion is not interesting.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective:_Negative_Polite_Form_20250209_彼の意見は面白くないです.mp3

examples.jp: その映画は楽しくありません。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa tanoshiku arimasen.

grammars.formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くないです
grammars.long_explanation: To make an い-adjective negative and polite, remove the final い and add くないです. An alternative more formal style is くありません. For example, 美味しい → 美味しくないです / 美味しくありません。
grammars.short_explanation: Change an い-adjective into a polite negative form with ～くないです (or ～くありません).
grammars.title: い-Adjective: Negative Polite Form

examples.en: This apple is sweet and delicious.

examples.jp: このリンゴは甘くて美味しいです。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo wa amakute oishii desu.

examples.en: She is kind and cute.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_て_i-Adjective_+_te_20250209_彼女は優しくてかわいいです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は優しくてかわいいです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yasashikute kawaii desu.

examples.en: The movie was interesting and moving.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_い-Adjective_て_i-Adjective_+_te_20250209_映画は面白くて感動的でした.mp3
examples.jp: 映画は面白くて感動的でした。
examples.romaji: Eiga wa omoshirokute kandouteki deshita.

examples.en: This room is spacious and bright.

examples.jp: この部屋は広くて明るいです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hirokute akarui desu.

grammars.formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くて + い-Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The い-Adjective て form is used to connect two or more い-adjectives when listing attributes of something or someone. To form it, replace the final い with くて. For example, かわいい → かわいくて, おいしい → おいしくて.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to connect two or more い-adjectives to describe something.
grammars.title: い-Adjective て (i-Adjective + te~)

examples.romaji: Kare wa shizuka ni hanasu.

examples.romaji: Heya o kirei ni souji shita.

grammars.formation: な-Adjective (remove な) + に + Verb
grammars.long_explanation: To make a な-adjective modify a verb, remove the な and add に. This form describes how an action is performed. For instance, 静か（な） → 静かに, 親切（な） → 親切に.
grammars.short_explanation: Turn a な-adjective into an adverb by adding に.
grammars.title: な-Adjective に + Verb

examples.romaji: Kono heya wa seiketsu de kimochi ga ii desu.

grammars.formation: な-Adjective + で
grammars.long_explanation: Use な-adjective + で to connect it to another quality, action, or description. It can combine a な-adjective with another adjective, verb, or clause.
grammars.short_explanation: Usage of で to connect or add information with a な-adjective.
grammars.title: な-Adjective で～ (na-Adjective de~)

examples.romaji: Heya o kirei ni shimasu.

grammars.formation: な-Adjective + に + します

grammars.short_explanation: Expressing a decision or preference with a な-adjective.
grammars.title: な-Adjective に します (na-Adjective ni shimasu)

grammars.short_explanation: Express a change or transformation into a state described by the な-adjective.
grammars.title: な-Adjective に なります (na-Adjective ni narimasu)

grammars.formation: Noun1 + から + Noun2 + まで
grammars.long_explanation: The から...まで grammar point is used to express a range between two nouns, indicating the starting point and ending point of an action, event, or period of time. It can be translated as 'from...to' or 'between...and' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses a range; 'from...to', 'between...and'.
grammars.title: Noun から Noun まで (Noun kara Noun made)

examples.en: This book has about 300 pages.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_くらい～_Noun_kurai～_20250209_この本は三百ページくらいあります.mp3
examples.jp: この本は三百ページくらいあります。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa sanbyaku peeji kurai arimasu.

examples.en: It takes about 20 minutes to walk to his house.

examples.romaji: Kare no ie made aruite nijuppun kurai kakarimasu.

examples.en: Tomorrow will be hot, about 30 degrees.

examples.jp: 明日は暑くて、30度くらいになるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa atsukute, sanjuu-do kurai ni naru deshou.

examples.en: You need about 500 yen worth of ingredients to make this dish.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_くらい～_Noun_kurai～_20250209_この料理を作るのに材料は500円くらい必要です.mp3
examples.jp: この料理を作るのに、材料は500円くらい必要です。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri o tsukuru no ni, zairyou wa gohyaku-en kurai hitsuyou desu.

grammars.formation: Noun + くらい
grammars.long_explanation: The くらい grammar point is used with a noun to express the extent or degree of something, meaning 'about', 'approximately', or 'at least' in English. It helps to provide a rough estimate or minimum standard to the noun it is attached to.
grammars.short_explanation: Express the extent or degree of something; 'about', 'approximately', 'at least'.
grammars.title: Noun くらい～ (Noun kurai～)

examples.en: I studied all day, so I studied for about 10 hours.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ぐらい～_Noun_gurai～_20250209_一日中勉強したので１０時間ぐらい勉強しました.mp3
examples.jp: 一日中勉強したので、１０時間ぐらい勉強しました。
examples.romaji: Ichinichijuu benkyou shita node, juu-jikan gurai benkyou shimashita.

examples.en: This book has about 100 pages.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ぐらい～_Noun_gurai～_20250209_この本は１００ページぐらいある.mp3
examples.jp: この本は１００ページぐらいある。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa hyaku peeji gurai aru.

examples.romaji: Kare wa kudamono o go-ko gurai tabemashita.

examples.en: It takes about 20 minutes to walk from the station to my house.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ぐらい～_Noun_gurai～_20250209_駅から家まで歩いて２０分ぐらいかかります.mp3
examples.jp: 駅から家まで歩いて２０分ぐらいかかります。
examples.romaji: Eki kara ie made aruite nijuppun gurai kakarimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + ぐらい
grammars.long_explanation: The ぐらい grammar point is used with nouns to express an approximate amount or degree. It is often translated as 'about', 'approximately', or 'around' in English. This can be used for time, quantity, or other measurements.
grammars.short_explanation: Express an approximate amount or degree; 'about', 'approximately'.
grammars.title: Noun ぐらい～ (Noun gurai～)

examples.en: Please call me around noon.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ごろ～_Noun_+_goro～_20250209_昼ごろに電話してください.mp3
examples.jp: 昼ごろに電話してください。
examples.romaji: Hiru goro ni denwa shite kudasai.

examples.en: He came to Japan around the age of 10.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ごろ～_Noun_+_goro～_20250209_彼は10歳ごろに日本に来ました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は10歳ごろに日本に来ました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa juu-sai goro ni Nihon ni kimashita.

examples.en: Let's meet around 3 PM.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ごろ～_Noun_+_goro～_20250209_午後３時ごろに会いましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 午後３時ごろに会いましょう。
examples.romaji: Gogo san-ji goro ni aimashou.

examples.en: I returned home last night around 8 o'clock.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_ごろ～_Noun_+_goro～_20250209_昨日の夜8時ごろに帰りました.mp3
examples.jp: 昨日の夜8時ごろに帰りました。
examples.romaji: Kinou no yoru hachi-ji goro ni kaerimashita.

grammars.formation: Noun + ごろ
grammars.long_explanation: The ごろ grammar point is used to indicate 'around' or 'about' a certain time or age. It is commonly used with time-related expressions and age-related expressions to give an approximate time or age.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'around' or 'about' a certain time or age.
grammars.title: Noun ごろ～ (Noun + goro～)

examples.en: I only drank coffee and went home.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_だけ_dake_20250209_コーヒーだけ飲んで帰りました.mp3
examples.jp: コーヒーだけ飲んで、帰りました。
examples.romaji: Koohii dake nonde, kaerimashita.

examples.en: I only read twenty pages of this book.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_だけ_dake_20250209_この本は二十ページだけ読んだ.mp3
examples.jp: この本は二十ページだけ読んだ。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa nijuu peeji dake yonda.

examples.en: She is very fast, not only at running but also at thinking.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_だけ_dake_20250209_彼女はとても速いですが走るだけでなく考えるのも速いです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はとても速いですが、走るだけでなく、考えるのも速いです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa totemo hayai desu ga, hashiru dake denaku, kangaeru no mo hayai desu.

examples.en: This room is a place only for sleeping.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_だけ_dake_20250209_この部屋は寝るだけの場所です.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋は寝るだけの場所です。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa neru dake no basho desu.

grammars.formation: Noun + だけ, Verb-casual + だけ, い-Adjective + だけ, な-Adjective-な + だけ
grammars.long_explanation: The Noun だけ grammar point is used to emphasize the idea of 'only', 'just', or 'merely' in a sentence. It can be attached to nouns, verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives to show this emphasis. This grammar point is commonly used in both spoken and written Japanese.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates 'only', 'just', or 'merely'.
grammars.title: Noun だけ〜 (〜dake)

examples.en: I study at the library.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Nounで～_Noun_de__20250209_図書館で勉強します.mp3
examples.jp: 図書館で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Toshokan de benkyou shimasu.

examples.en: I go to school by bus.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Nounで～_Noun_de__20250209_バスで学校に行きます.mp3
examples.jp: バスで学校に行きます。
examples.romaji: Basu de gakkou ni ikimasu.

examples.en: I wrote it using a pencil.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Nounで～_Noun_de__20250209_鉛筆で書きました.mp3
examples.jp: 鉛筆で書きました。
examples.romaji: Enpitsu de kakimashita.

examples.en: Let's talk in English.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Nounで～_Noun_de__20250209_英語で話しましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 英語で話しましょう。
examples.romaji: Eigo de hanashimashou.

grammars.formation: Noun + で
grammars.long_explanation: The で grammar point is used to indicate a location, method, or tool for doing an action or for being in a situation. It can be translated as 'at, in, on', 'using', or 'by means of' in English. Nounで is formed by adding で after a noun.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicate a place or means for an action or situation; 'at, in, on', 'using', or 'by means of'.
grammars.title: Nounで～ (Noun de ~)

examples.en: I bought apples and bananas.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_と～_Noun_to～_20250209_リンゴとバナナを買いました.mp3
examples.jp: リンゴとバナナを買いました。
examples.romaji: Ringo to banana wo kaimashita.

examples.en: I will go to watch a movie with my friend.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_と～_Noun_to～_20250209_友達と映画を見に行きます.mp3
examples.jp: 友達と映画を見に行きます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi to eiga wo mi ni ikimasu.

examples.en: I traveled together with my father and mother.

examples.jp: 父と母と一緒に旅行しました。
examples.romaji: Chichi to haha to issho ni ryokou shimashita.

examples.en: He and she got married.

examples.jp: 彼と彼女は結婚しました。
examples.romaji: Kare to kanojo wa kekkon shimashita.

grammars.formation: Noun1 + と + Noun2
grammars.long_explanation: The Noun と grammar point is used to express a connection between two or more nouns, indicating 'with', 'and', or 'together with' in English. It functions as a particle that is used to simply list multiple items or express companionship.
grammars.short_explanation: Express 'with', 'and' or 'together with' when connecting nouns.
grammars.title: Noun と～ (Noun to～)

examples.en: I gave a present to her.

examples.jp: 彼女にプレゼントをあげました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ni purezento wo agemashita.

examples.en: I am going to Japan.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に～_Noun_ni～_20250209_日本に行きます.mp3
examples.jp: 日本に行きます。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni ikimasu.

examples.jp: 6時に集合しましょう。
examples.romaji: Roku-ji ni shuugou shimashou.

examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni tegami wo kakimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に
grammars.long_explanation: The 'Noun に' grammar point is used to express a specific direction, target, or purpose in relation to a noun. It can be translated as 'to', 'toward', or 'for' in English. The に particle is added directly after the noun which indicates direction, target or purpose.
grammars.short_explanation: Express a specific direction, target or purpose; 'to', 'toward', 'for'.
grammars.title: Noun に～ (Noun ni～)

examples.en: When summer vacation ends, I'll go back to school.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_帰ります_Noun_ni_kaerimasu_20250209_夏休みが終わったら学校に帰ります.mp3
examples.jp: 夏休みが終わったら、学校に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Natsuyasumi ga owattara, gakkou ni kaerimasu.

examples.en: After finishing shopping, I will go back home.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_帰ります_Noun_ni_kaerimasu_20250209_買い物を終えたら家に帰ります.mp3
examples.jp: 買い物を終えたら、家に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o oetara, ie ni kaerimasu.

examples.en: I'm going back to my parents' home this weekend.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_帰ります_Noun_ni_kaerimasu_20250209_今週末実家に帰ります.mp3
examples.jp: 今週末、実家に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Konshuumatsu, jikka ni kaerimasu.

examples.en: After traveling with my friend, I'll return to Tokyo.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_帰ります_Noun_ni_kaerimasu_20250209_友達と旅行に行ったあと東京に帰ります.mp3
examples.jp: 友達と旅行に行ったあと、東京に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi to ryokou ni itta ato, Toukyou ni kaerimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に + 帰ります
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point 'Noun に 帰ります' is used to express physically going back or returning to a specific place. It can be translated as 'to go back to' or 'to return to' in English. The particle に indicates the destination of the return.
grammars.short_explanation: Express going back or returning to a place: 'to return to', 'to go back to'.
grammars.title: Noun に 帰ります (Noun ni kaerimasu)

examples.en: I'll choose sushi for today's lunch.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_します_Noun_ni_shimasu_20250209_今日の昼ご飯は寿司にします.mp3
examples.jp: 今日の昼ご飯は寿司にします。
examples.romaji: Kyou no hirugohan wa sushi ni shimasu.

examples.en: I was hesitating about which shoes to buy, but I'll go with the red ones.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_します_Noun_ni_shimasu_20250209_この靴を買うか迷っていますが赤い色の方にします.mp3
examples.jp: この靴を買うか迷っていますが、赤い色の方にします。
examples.romaji: Kono kutsu wo kau ka mayotteimasu ga, akai iro no hou ni shimasu.

examples.en: I've decided what to do on my day off. I'll go to the movie theater.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_します_Noun_ni_shimasu_20250209_休みの日に何をするか決めた映画館に行くことにします.mp3
examples.jp: 休みの日に何をするか決めた。映画館に行くことにします。
examples.romaji: Yasumi no hi ni nani wo suru ka kimeta. Eigakan ni iku koto ni shimasu.

examples.en: I was torn between studying French and Spanish, but I decided on French.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_します_Noun_ni_shimasu_20250209_フランス語とスペイン語のどちらを勉強するか悩んだがフランス語にします.mp3
examples.jp: フランス語とスペイン語のどちらを勉強するか悩んだが、フランス語にします。
examples.romaji: Furansugo to Supeingo no dochira wo benkyou suru ka nayanda ga, Furansugo ni shimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に します
grammars.long_explanation: The に します grammar point is used to express making a choice or decision. It can be translated as 'choose' or 'decide on' in English. It is often used in situations where someone has to make a selection or decide on something, such as ordering food at a restaurant or deciding on a vacation destination.
grammars.short_explanation: Express a choice or decision; 'choose', 'decide on'.
grammars.title: Noun に します (Noun ni shimasu)

examples.en: He will become a doctor.

examples.romaji: Kare wa isha ni narimasu.

examples.romaji: Kono chairo no ha ga aka ni narimasu.

examples.romaji: Ryouri ga sametara, oishikunaku narimasu.

examples.en: Next year, it will be the Tokyo Olympics.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_に_なります_Noun_ni_narimasu_20250209_来年東京オリンピックになります.mp3
examples.jp: 来年、東京オリンピックになります。
examples.romaji: Rainen, Toukyou Orinpikku ni narimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に + なります
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point Noun に なります is used to express a change or transformation into something else, or to indicate that something 'becomes', 'turns into', or simply 'is' something. It is commonly used with nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses change or becoming something; 'to become', 'to turn into', 'to be'.
grammars.title: Noun に なります (Noun ni narimasu)

examples.en: My friend will come to my house.

examples.romaji: Konban, chichi ga eki ni mukae ni kimasu.

examples.en: Tomorrow, the teacher will come to school.

examples.romaji: Ashita, sensei ga gakkou ni kimasu.

examples.en: A famous singer will come to this town.

examples.romaji: Yuumei na kashu ga kono machi ni kimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に + 来ます (kimasu)
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point Noun に 来ます is used to indicate that someone or something comes to a specific place. The noun before に indicates the destination or place, while the verb 来ます expresses the action of coming. (Similarly, 'Noun に 行きます' means 'go to [Noun],' and 'Noun に 帰ります' means 'return to [Noun].')
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express coming to a place.
grammars.title: Noun に 来ます (Noun ni kimasu)

examples.en: I will go to the movie theater on the weekend.

examples.romaji: Shuumatsu ni eigakan ni ikimasu.

examples.romaji: Natsu yasumi ni umi ni ikimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + に + 行きます
grammars.long_explanation: The Noun に 行きます grammar point is used to express going to a specific location. This structure requires a noun (indicating the destination) followed by に and the verb 行きます, which means 'to go'.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express going to a location.
grammars.title: Noun に 行きます (Noun ni ikimasu)

examples.en: After dinner, I went for a walk.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_の_あとで_Noun_no_atode_20250209_晩ご飯のあとで散歩に行きました.mp3
examples.jp: 晩ご飯のあとで、散歩に行きました。
examples.romaji: Bangohan no atode, sanpo ni ikimashita.

grammars.formation: Noun + の + あとで
grammars.long_explanation: The の あとで grammar point is used to express the order of events, specifying that an action occurs after or later than the noun mentioned. It translates to 'after' or 'later than' in English. This structure is simply formed by attaching の あとで to the noun.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses the order of events; 'after', 'later than'.
grammars.title: Noun の あとで (Noun no atode)

examples.en: There is a convenience store in front of the station.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_の_前に_Noun_no_mae_ni_20250209_駅の前にコンビニがあります.mp3
examples.jp: 駅の前にコンビニがあります。
examples.romaji: Eki no mae ni konbini ga arimasu.

examples.en: Please park the car in front of the house.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_の_前に_Noun_no_mae_ni_20250209_家の前に車を止めてください.mp3
examples.jp: 家の前に車を止めてください。
examples.romaji: Ie no mae ni kuruma wo tomete kudasai.

examples.en: He was standing in front of me.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_の_前に_Noun_no_mae_ni_20250209_私の前に彼が立っていました.mp3
examples.jp: 私の前に彼が立っていました。
examples.romaji: Watashi no mae ni kare ga tatte imashita.

examples.en: A taxi came in front of the hotel.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_の_前に_Noun_no_mae_ni_20250209_ホテルの前にタクシーが来た.mp3
examples.jp: ホテルの前にタクシーが来た。
examples.romaji: Hoteru no mae ni takushii ga kita.

grammars.formation: Noun + の + 前に
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point Noun の 前に is used to describe a location or position 'in front of' a noun. It is formed by adding の 前に after the noun it refers to. (Note that 'Noun の 前に' can also mean 'before [Noun]' in time contexts, but these examples focus on physical location.)
grammars.short_explanation: Used to describe a location or position 'in front of' a noun.
grammars.title: Noun の 前に (Noun no mae ni)

examples.en: As for me, I like Japanese cuisine.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_は～_Noun_wa_20250209_私は日本の料理が好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 私は日本の料理が好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa Nihon no ryouri ga suki desu.

examples.en: As for him, he is good at English.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_は～_Noun_wa_20250209_彼は英語が上手です.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は英語が上手です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo ga jouzu desu.

examples.en: As for this book, it's interesting.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_は～_Noun_wa_20250209_この本は面白いです.mp3
examples.jp: この本は面白いです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa omoshiroi desu.

examples.en: Speaking of today, it's hot, isn't it?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_は～_Noun_wa_20250209_今日は暑いですね.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は暑いですね。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa atsui desu ne.

grammars.formation: Noun + は
grammars.long_explanation: The は (wa) particle is used to indicate the topic of a sentence. It is usually translated as 'as for', 'speaking of', or it simply marks what the sentence is about. This is different from が (ga), which marks the subject of a verb.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to mark the topic of a sentence; 'as for', 'speaking of'.
grammars.title: Noun は～ (Noun wa〜)

examples.en: I am also studying Japanese.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_も_Noun_mo_20250209_私も日本語を勉強しています.mp3
examples.jp: 私も日本語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Watashi mo nihongo wo benkyou shiteimasu.

examples.en: He also likes cake.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_も_Noun_mo_20250209_彼もケーキが好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼もケーキが好きです。
examples.romaji: Kare mo keeki ga suki desu.

examples.en: There are many tourist spots in both Tokyo and Osaka.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_も_Noun_mo_20250209_東京も大阪も観光スポットがたくさんあります.mp3
examples.jp: 東京も大阪も観光スポットがたくさんあります。
examples.romaji: Toukyou mo Oosaka mo kankou supotto ga takusan arimasu.

examples.en: Both this movie and that movie were interesting.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_も_Noun_mo_20250209_この映画もあの映画も面白かった.mp3
examples.jp: この映画もあの映画も面白かった。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga mo ano eiga mo omoshirokatta.

grammars.formation: Noun + も
grammars.long_explanation: The も grammar point is used after a noun to indicate that the action or state is the same for multiple items or people. It means 'also', 'as well', or 'too' in English. も often replaces は or が in the sentence to show that the same statement applies to this additional noun.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates that the action or state is the same for multiple items or people; 'also', 'as well'.
grammars.title: Noun も〜 (Noun mo~)

examples.en: He likes to eat things like vegetables and fruits.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_や_Noun_など～_Noun_ya_Noun_nado_20250209_彼は野菜や果物などを食べるのが好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は野菜や果物などを食べるのが好きです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yasai ya kudamono nado o taberu no ga suki desu.

examples.en: I want to go to Japanese cities such as Tokyo, Osaka, and so on.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_や_Noun_など～_Noun_ya_Noun_nado_20250209_日本の都市や東京大阪などに行きたいです.mp3
examples.jp: 日本の都市や東京、大阪などに行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Nihon no toshi ya Toukyou, Oosaka nado ni ikitai desu.

examples.en: She likes animals like cats, dogs, and so on.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_や_Noun_など～_Noun_ya_Noun_nado_20250209_彼女は猫や犬など動物が好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は猫や犬など動物が好きです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa neko ya inu nado doubutsu ga suki desu.

examples.en: In this bookstore, many books such as manga and novels are sold.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_や_Noun_など～_Noun_ya_Noun_nado_20250209_この本屋では漫画や小説などたくさんの本が売られています.mp3
examples.jp: この本屋では漫画や小説などたくさんの本が売られています。
examples.romaji: Kono honya de wa manga ya shousetsu nado takusan no hon ga urarete imasu.

grammars.formation: Noun1 + や + Noun2 + など
grammars.long_explanation: The や...など grammar point is used to list a few items or examples that belong to a similar category or context, but it is not exhaustive. It can be translated as 'such as', 'like', or 'and so on' in English. This grammar pattern is used with nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: Lists items or examples but not exhaustively; 'such as', 'like', 'and so on'.
grammars.title: Noun や Noun など～ (Noun ya Noun nado)

examples.en: I read a book.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_を_Noun_wo_20250209_私は本を読みます.mp3
examples.jp: 私は本を読みます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa hon wo yomimasu.

examples.en: He ate a cake.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_を_Noun_wo_20250209_彼はケーキを食べました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はケーキを食べました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa keeki wo tabemashita.

examples.en: My mother likes to drink coffee.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_を_Noun_wo_20250209_母はコーヒーを飲むのが好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 母はコーヒーを飲むのが好きです。
examples.romaji: Haha wa koohii wo nomu no ga suki desu.

examples.en: My friend used my pen.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Noun_を_Noun_wo_20250209_友達が私のペンを使いました.mp3
examples.jp: 友達が私のペンを使いました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi no pen wo tsukaimashita.

grammars.formation: Noun + を + Verb
grammars.long_explanation: The を (wo) particle is used to mark the direct object of a verb in a sentence. It shows the noun that the action (verb) is performed on. The particle を is usually pronounced as 'o' in spoken Japanese.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates the direct object of a verb.
grammars.title: Noun を〜 (Noun wo〜)

examples.en: After doing my homework, I watched TV.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_た_あとで_ta_ato_de_20250209_宿題をしたあとでテレビを見ました.mp3
examples.jp: 宿題をしたあとで、テレビを見ました。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo shita ato de, terebi wo mimashita.

examples.en: After eating breakfast, I brush my teeth.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_た_あとで_ta_ato_de_20250209_朝ごはんを食べたあとで歯を磨きます.mp3
examples.jp: 朝ごはんを食べたあとで、歯を磨きます。
examples.romaji: Asagohan wo tabeta ato de, ha wo migakimasu.

examples.en: After finishing work, I plan to go to the gym.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_た_あとで_ta_ato_de_20250209_仕事が終わったあとでジムに行く予定です.mp3
examples.jp: 仕事が終わったあとで、ジムに行く予定です。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owatta ato de, jimu ni iku yotei desu.

examples.en: After watching the movie, I drank coffee at a cafe.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_た_あとで_ta_ato_de_20250209_映画を見たあとでカフェでコーヒーを飲みました.mp3
examples.jp: 映画を見たあとで、カフェでコーヒーを飲みました。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mita ato de, kafe de koohii wo nomimashita.

grammars.formation: Verb-た form + あとで
grammars.long_explanation: The たあとで grammar point is used to indicate that one action takes place after another action is completed. It means 'after' or 'after doing' in English. The formation is created with the た form (past tense) of a verb, followed by あとで (ato de).
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates an action that takes place after another action.
grammars.title: Verb た あとで (ta ato de)

examples.en: I want to eat sushi.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_たいです_taidesu_20250209_私は寿司を食べたいです.mp3
examples.jp: 私は寿司を食べたいです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa sushi wo tabetai desu.

examples.en: He wants to go to Japan.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_たいです_taidesu_20250209_彼は日本に行きたいです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は日本に行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa Nihon ni ikitai desu.

examples.en: She wants to study English.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_たいです_taidesu_20250209_彼女は英語を勉強したいです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は英語を勉強したいです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo wo benkyou shitai desu.

examples.en: The children want to play.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_たいです_taidesu_20250209_子供たちは遊びたいです.mp3
examples.jp: 子供たちは遊びたいです。
examples.romaji: Kodomo-tachi wa asobitai desu.

grammars.formation: る-Verb: Remove る and add たいです, う-Verb: Replace the final verb character with the ～い form and add たいです, Exception: する becomes したいです
grammars.long_explanation: The たいです grammar point is used to express the speaker's desire or want to perform a certain action. It can be translated as 'I want to' or 'I would like to' in English. The formation differs depending on whether the verb is a る-verb or an う-verb.
grammars.short_explanation: Express desire or want to do something; 'I want to', 'I would like to'.
grammars.title: Verb たいです (taidesu)

examples.en: After drinking coffee, I will go out.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て～_Verb_+_te～_20250209_コーヒーを飲んで出かけます.mp3
examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、出かけます。
examples.romaji: Koohii o nonde, dekakemasu.

examples.en: Let's go shopping and then go home.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て～_Verb_+_te～_20250209_買い物をして家に帰りましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 買い物をして、家に帰りましょう。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o shite, ie ni kaerimashou.

examples.en: After doing my homework, I will sleep.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て～_Verb_+_te～_20250209_宿題をして寝ます.mp3
examples.jp: 宿題をして、寝ます。
examples.romaji: Shukudai o shite, nemasu.

examples.en: I will wait for my friend and go watch a movie together.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て～_Verb_+_te～_20250209_友達を待って一緒に映画を見に行きます.mp3
examples.jp: 友達を待って、一緒に映画を見に行きます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi o matte, issho ni eiga o mini ikimasu.

grammars.formation: Verb (Group 1) - Replace last syllable with 〜て, Verb (Group 2) - Replace 'る' with 〜て, Verb (Group 3) - する becomes して, くる becomes きて
grammars.long_explanation: The ～て form of a verb is used to connect actions or states in a sequence, implying that the first action is completed before the second one starts. The ～て form is frequently used in casual speech, and it can also be used in polite speech when combined with certain auxiliary verbs like ください (kudasai) or いる (iru).
grammars.short_explanation: A verb conjugation that connects actions or states.
grammars.title: Verb て～ (Verb + te～)

examples.en: She is playing the piano now.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_います_Verb_te_imasu_20250209_彼女は今ピアノを弾いています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は今ピアノを弾いています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa ima piano wo hiite imasu.

examples.en: We are studying Japanese.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_います_Verb_te_imasu_20250209_私たちは日本語を勉強しています.mp3
examples.jp: 私たちは日本語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa nihongo wo benkyou shiteimasu.

examples.en: He is watching a movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_います_Verb_te_imasu_20250209_彼は映画を見ています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は映画を見ています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eiga wo miteimasu.

examples.en: I am in, so please wait.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_います_Verb_te_imasu_20250209_入っていますのでお待ちください.mp3
examples.jp: 入っていますので、お待ちください。
examples.romaji: Haitteimasu node, omachi kudasai.

grammars.formation: Verb て-form + います
grammars.long_explanation: The て います grammar point is used to express an action that is ongoing, continuous, or has been happening. It is formed by conjugating the verb in its て-form and adding います. It can be translated as 'is doing', 'is doing (continuous)', or 'has been doing' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Express ongoing action or state; 'is doing', 'is doing (continuous)', 'has been doing'.
grammars.title: Verb て います (Verb te imasu)

examples.en: I watched TV after doing my homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_てから～_te_kara_20250209_宿題をしてからテレビを見ました.mp3

examples.romaji: Shukudai wo shite kara, terebi wo mimashita.

examples.en: Let's brush our teeth after eating.

examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owatte kara, tomodachi to nomi ni ikimasu.

examples.en: I will study in the library after school is over.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_てから～_te_kara_20250209_学校が終わってから図書館で勉強します.mp3
examples.jp: 学校が終わってから、図書館で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Gakkou ga owatte kara, toshokan de benkyou shimasu.

grammars.formation: Verb-て形 + から
grammars.long_explanation: The ～てから grammar point is used to indicate the sequence of actions or events, meaning that one action or event occurs after another. It can be translated as 'after', 'since', or 'once' in English. The て-form indicates the first action and から shows the sequence.
grammars.short_explanation: Express a sequence of actions or events; 'after', 'since', 'once'.
grammars.title: Verb てから～ (〜te kara)

examples.jp: ドアを開けてください。
examples.romaji: Doa wo akete kudasai.

examples.en: Please tell me your phone number.

examples.jp: 電話番号を教えてください。
examples.romaji: Denwa bangou wo oshiete kudasai.

examples.en: Please speak slowly.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_ください_Verb-te_kudasai_20250209_ゆっくり話してください.mp3
examples.jp: ゆっくり話してください。
examples.romaji: Yukkuri hanashite kudasai.

examples.en: Please bring me a coffee.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_て_ください_Verb-te_kudasai_20250209_コーヒーを一つ持ってきてください.mp3
examples.jp: コーヒーを一つ持ってきてください。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo hitotsu motte kite kudasai.

grammars.formation: Verb-て form + ください
grammars.long_explanation: The て ください grammar point is used to make a request or command someone to do something politely. The verb is conjugated into its て-form and followed by ください, which means 'please'. This structure is used when asking someone to do something with a polite and respectful tone.
grammars.short_explanation: A request or command; 'please do'.
grammars.title: Verb て ください (Verb-te kudasai)

examples.en: Please don't smoke.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_ないで_ください_naide_kudasai_20250209_タバコを吸わないでください.mp3

examples.romaji: Tabako wo suwanaide kudasai.

examples.en: Please don't run here.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_ないで_ください_naide_kudasai_20250209_ここで走らないでください.mp3
examples.jp: ここで走らないでください。
examples.romaji: Koko de hashiranaide kudasai.

examples.en: Please don't speak loudly.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_ないで_ください_naide_kudasai_20250209_大きな声で話さないでください.mp3
examples.jp: 大きな声で話さないでください。
examples.romaji: Ookina koe de hanasanaide kudasai.

examples.en: Please don't take photos.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_Verb_ないで_ください_naide_kudasai_20250209_写真を撮らないでください.mp3
examples.jp: 写真を撮らないでください。
examples.romaji: Shashin wo toranaide kudasai.

grammars.formation: Verb-ない-form + で ください
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point Verb ないで ください is used to make a polite request for someone not to do a certain action. In English, it can be translated as 'please don't'. To form this expression, take the verb in its negative form (ない-form) and add で ください.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to make a polite request for someone not to do something; 'please don't'.
grammars.title: Verb ないで ください (〜naide kudasai)

examples.en: When put in the refrigerator, the melted ice cream returns to its solid state.

grammars.short_explanation: Used to make a polite suggestion or offer help; 'shall we', 'should we', 'do you want me to'.

grammars.short_explanation: Express an action or event as a noun; 'the act of', 'doing'.

examples.romaji: Ie no naka ni furui terebi ga arimasu.

grammars.formation: Object + が + あります
grammars.long_explanation: The あります grammar point is used to indicate the possession or existence of inanimate objects. It can be translated as 'there is' or 'there are' in English. It is different from います, which is used for people and most living creatures. あります is commonly used with particle が to mark the object.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicate possession or existence of inanimate objects; 'there is', 'there are'.
grammars.title: ～あります (〜arimasu)

examples.en: How about some tea?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～いかがですか_ikaga_desu_ka_20250209_お茶はいかがですか.mp3
examples.jp: お茶はいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Ocha wa ikaga desu ka?

examples.en: How about this dress?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～いかがですか_ikaga_desu_ka_20250209_このドレスはいかがですか.mp3
examples.jp: このドレスはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Kono doresu wa ikaga desu ka?

examples.en: How about eating some cake?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～いかがですか_ikaga_desu_ka_20250209_ケーキを食べてはいかがですか.mp3
examples.jp: ケーキを食べてはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Keeki wo tabete wa ikaga desu ka?

examples.en: How about watching a movie?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～いかがですか_ikaga_desu_ka_20250209_映画を見てはいかがですか.mp3
examples.jp: 映画を見てはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mite wa ikaga desu ka?

grammars.formation: Noun + は + いかがですか / (Verb-て form + は) いかがですか
grammars.long_explanation: The ～いかがですか grammar point is used to politely ask someone's thoughts, opinions, or preferences. It can be translated as 'how about' or 'how is' in English. The formation is quite straightforward when used with verbs or nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: A polite way to ask someone's thoughts, opinions, or preferences; 'how about', 'how is'.
grammars.title: ～いかがですか。 (〜ikaga desu ka.)

examples.en: How many apples are there?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いくつ～_ikutsu_20250209_リンゴはいくつありますか.mp3
examples.jp: リンゴはいくつありますか？
examples.romaji: Ringo wa ikutsu arimasu ka?

examples.en: I have to solve several problems.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いくつ～_ikutsu_20250209_いくつかの問題を解決しなければなりません.mp3
examples.jp: いくつかの問題を解決しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Ikutsu ka no mondai o kaiketsu shinakereba narimasen.

examples.en: How many languages can you speak?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いくつ～_ikutsu_20250209_あなたはいくつの言語を話せますか.mp3
examples.jp: あなたはいくつの言語を話せますか？
examples.romaji: Anata wa ikutsu no gengo o hanasemasu ka?

examples.en: There are several drinks at the party.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いくつ～_ikutsu_20250209_パーティーにはいくつかの飲み物があります.mp3
examples.jp: パーティーにはいくつかの飲み物があります。
examples.romaji: Paatii ni wa ikutsu ka no nomimono ga arimasu.

grammars.formation: いくつ + Noun (optional)
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point いくつ is used when asking or expressing 'how many' of something there are, or to indicate an unspecified number. In English, it can be translated as 'how many' or 'several'.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'how many' or ask for the number of something.
grammars.title: いくつ～ (ikutsu~)

examples.en: I want to go to Japan someday.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつか～_itsuka～_20250209_いつか日本に行きたいです.mp3
examples.jp: いつか日本に行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Itsuka Nihon ni ikitai desu.

examples.en: He will become a famous writer someday.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつか～_itsuka～_20250209_彼はいつか有名な作家になるでしょう.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はいつか有名な作家になるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kare wa itsuka yuumei na sakka ni naru deshou.

examples.en: I think I want to climb that mountain someday.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつか～_itsuka～_20250209_いつかあの山を登りたいと思っています.mp3
examples.jp: いつかあの山を登りたいと思っています。
examples.romaji: Itsuka ano yama wo noboritai to omotte imasu.

examples.en: I believe she can achieve her dream someday.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつか～_itsuka～_20250209_彼女はいつか夢を叶えることができると信じています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はいつか夢を叶えることができると信じています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsuka yume wo kanaeru koto ga dekiru to shinjiteimasu.

grammars.formation: いつか + sentence
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point いつか is used to indicate an unspecified point in time, meaning 'someday', 'one day', or 'at some point' in the future or the past. It can be used in sentences to express hopes, dreams, or possibilities.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates an unspecified point in time; 'someday', 'one day', 'at some point'.
grammars.title: いつか～ (itsuka～)

examples.en: Please come to play anytime.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつでも～_itsudemo～_20250209_いつでも遊びに来てください.mp3
examples.jp: いつでも遊びに来てください。
examples.romaji: Itsudemo asobi ni kite kudasai.

examples.en: She is always smiling.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつでも～_itsudemo～_20250209_彼女はいつでも笑顔です.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はいつでも笑顔です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsudemo egao desu.

examples.en: You can contact me by phone anytime.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつでも～_itsudemo～_20250209_いつでも電話で連絡できます.mp3
examples.jp: いつでも電話で連絡できます。
examples.romaji: Itsudemo denwa de renraku dekimasu.

examples.en: This store is always crowded.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつでも～_itsudemo～_20250209_この店はいつでも混んでいます.mp3
examples.jp: この店はいつでも混んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa itsudemo konde imasu.

grammars.formation: いつでも + (Verb)
grammars.long_explanation: The いつでも grammar point is used to express that something occurs, can occur, or is allowed to occur anytime, always, or whenever. It emphasizes the lack of restrictions related to time for a certain action or event.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'anytime', 'always', or 'whenever'.
grammars.title: いつでも～ (itsudemo～)

examples.en: He is always late.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつも～_itsumo～_20250209_彼はいつも遅刻します.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はいつも遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kare wa itsumo chikoku shimasu.

examples.en: I always like gentle dogs.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつも～_itsumo～_20250209_私はいつも優しい犬が好きです.mp3
examples.jp: 私はいつも優しい犬が好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa itsumo yasashii inu ga suki desu.

examples.en: She always studies in a quiet place.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつも～_itsumo～_20250209_彼女はいつも静かな場所で勉強します.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はいつも静かな場所で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsumo shizuka na basho de benkyou shimasu.

examples.en: I always eat breakfast.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_いつも～_itsumo～_20250209_いつも朝ご飯を食べます.mp3
examples.jp: いつも朝ご飯を食べます。
examples.romaji: Itsumo asagohan wo tabemasu.

grammars.formation: いつも + Verb / Adjective / Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point いつも (itsumo) is used to express the meaning of 'always' or 'usually' when describing a habitual action or situation. It is often used with the present tense or past tense to show that something is done on a regular basis or has been happening consistently.
grammars.short_explanation: Expressing 'always' or 'usually' in a sentence.
grammars.title: いつも～ (itsumo～)

examples.en: I am listening to music right now.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～て_います_～te_imasu_20250209_今音楽を聞いています.mp3
examples.jp: 今、音楽を聞いています。
examples.romaji: Ima, ongaku wo kiite imasu.

examples.en: My father is reading a newspaper.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～て_います_～te_imasu_20250209_父は新聞を読んでいます.mp3
examples.jp: 父は新聞を読んでいます。
examples.romaji: Chichi wa shinbun wo yonde imasu.

examples.en: She is studying English.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～て_います_～te_imasu_20250209_彼女は英語を勉強しています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は英語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo wo benkyou shite imasu.

examples.en: The children are playing in the park.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～て_います_～te_imasu_20250209_子供たちは公園で遊んでいます.mp3
examples.jp: 子供たちは公園で遊んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kodomotachi wa kouen de asonde imasu.

grammars.formation: Verb て-form + います
grammars.long_explanation: The ～て います grammar pattern is used to express that an action is currently happening or ongoing. It can be translated as 'to be doing' or 'currently doing' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is a る-verb, う-verb, or an irregular verb, but all use the verb’s て-form + います.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses the present continuous or ongoing action; 'to be doing', 'currently doing'.
grammars.title: ～て います (～te imasu)

examples.en: I am a student.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_ga_20250209_私が学生です.mp3
examples.jp: 私が学生です。
examples.romaji: Watashi ga gakusei desu.

examples.en: This apple is delicious.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_ga_20250209_このりんごが美味しい.mp3
examples.jp: このりんごが美味しい。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo ga oishii.

examples.en: He is smart but has a bad personality.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_ga_20250209_彼は頭がいいが性格が悪い.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は頭がいいが、性格が悪い。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii ga, seikaku ga warui.

examples.en: I want to run, but my leg hurts.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_ga_20250209_走りたいが足が痛い.mp3
examples.jp: 走りたいが、足が痛い。
examples.romaji: Hashiritai ga, ashi ga itai.

grammars.formation: Noun + が / い-Adjective + が / な-Adjective + が / Verb + が
grammars.long_explanation: The ～が grammar point is a particle that is used to indicate the subject of a sentence or to express a contrast similar to 'but' in English. It has various functions depending on the context.
grammars.short_explanation: Particle indicating the subject of a sentence or expressing 'but'.
grammars.title: ～が (〜ga)

examples.en: The dessert is delicious, but it is high in calories.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が～_ga__20250209_デザートは美味しいがカロリーが高い.mp3
examples.jp: デザートは美味しいが、カロリーが高い。
examples.romaji: Dezaato wa oishii ga, karorii ga takai.

examples.en: He is smart, but a bit lazy.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が～_ga__20250209_彼は頭がいいが少し怠け者だ.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は頭がいいが、少し怠け者だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii ga, sukoshi namakemono da.

examples.en: The company made a profit, however, the employees' salaries did not increase.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が～_ga__20250209_会社は利益を上げたが従業員の給与は上がらなかった.mp3
examples.jp: 会社は利益を上げたが、従業員の給与は上がらなかった。
examples.romaji: Kaisha wa rieki wo ageta ga, juugyouin no kyuuyo wa agaranakatta.

examples.en: Studying foreign languages is fun, but sometimes difficult.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が～_ga__20250209_外国語を勉強することが楽しいが時々難しい.mp3
examples.jp: 外国語を勉強することが楽しいが、時々難しい。
examples.romaji: Gaikokugo wo benkyou suru koto ga tanoshii ga, tokidoki muzukashii.

grammars.formation: Sentence 1 + が、+ Sentence 2
grammars.long_explanation: The ～が、～ grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two sentences or clauses. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however' in English. This grammar point is slightly more formal than けど and is used to show a contrast in the situation.
grammars.short_explanation: Express a contrast between two sentences; 'but', 'however'.
grammars.title: ～が、～ (〜ga, 〜)

examples.en: Because I have an exam tomorrow, I must study tonight.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から～_kara～_20250209_明日は試験があるから今晩勉強しなければなりません.mp3
examples.jp: 明日は試験があるから、今晩勉強しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa shiken ga aru kara, konban benkyou shinakereba narimasen.

examples.en: Since this room is small, I am looking for a bigger one.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から～_kara～_20250209_この部屋は狭いからもっと大きい部屋を探しています.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋は狭いから、もっと大きい部屋を探しています。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa semai kara, motto ookii heya wo sagashiteimasu.

examples.en: Since he is my friend, he will probably help me.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から～_kara～_20250209_彼は友達だから手伝ってくれるでしょう.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は友達だから、手伝ってくれるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tomodachi dakara, tetsudatte kureru deshou.

examples.en: Because it rained, I can't go outside.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から～_kara～_20250209_雨が降ったから外に出られません.mp3
examples.jp: 雨が降ったから、外に出られません。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futta kara, soto ni deraremasen.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual + から / い-Adjective + から / な-Adjective + だから / Noun + だから
grammars.long_explanation: The ～から grammar point is used to indicate the reason or cause for something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
grammars.title: ～から、～ (〜kara、～)

examples.en: It’s because it’s cold. That’s why I’m wearing a coat.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～からです_kara_desu_20250209_寒いからですコートを着ています.mp3
examples.jp: 寒いからです。コートを着ています。
examples.romaji: Samui kara desu. Kooto wo kiteimasu.

examples.en: It’s because this store is cheap. That’s why I come often.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～からです_kara_desu_20250209_この店は安いからですよく来ます.mp3
examples.jp: この店は安いからです。よく来ます。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa yasui kara desu. Yoku kimasu.

examples.en: It’s because he’s kind. Everyone likes him.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～からです_kara_desu_20250209_彼は親切だからですみんなに好かれています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は親切だからです。みんなに好かれています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu dakara desu. Minna ni suka-rete imasu.

examples.en: It’s because she’s a student. She studies at the library.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～からです_kara_desu_20250209_彼女は学生だからです図書館で勉強しています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は学生だからです。図書館で勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei dakara desu. Toshokan de benkyou shiteimasu.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual + からです / い-Adjective + からです / な-Adjective + だからです / Noun + だからです
grammars.long_explanation: The ～からです grammar point is used to state the reason or cause of something, often as a short concluding statement. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to' in English. The formation can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns, but be careful with な-adjectives and nouns: typically, it's [Noun/な-adjective] + だからです.
grammars.short_explanation: Express the reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
grammars.title: ～からです (〜kara desu)

examples.en: I received a present from my friend.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から_もらいます_kara_moraimasu_20250209_友達からプレゼントをもらいました.mp3

examples.romaji: Tomodachi kara purezento wo moraimashita.

examples.en: I had the teacher hand me the homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から_もらいます_kara_moraimasu_20250209_先生に宿題を渡してもらいました.mp3
