examples.romaji: Sensei ni shukudai wo watashite moraimashita.

examples.en: I got my mom to cook for me.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から_もらいます_kara_moraimasu_20250209_お母さんに料理を作ってもらいました.mp3
examples.jp: お母さんに料理を作ってもらいました。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ni ryouri wo tsukutte moraimashita.

examples.en: I got my older brother to lend me his car.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～から_もらいます_kara_moraimasu_20250209_兄に車を貸してもらいました.mp3
examples.jp: 兄に車を貸してもらいました。
examples.romaji: Ani ni kuruma wo kashite moraimashita.

grammars.formation: Noun + から + (Verb-て form) + もらいます
grammars.long_explanation: The ～からもらいます grammar point is used to express receiving something from someone or getting someone to do something for you. In English, it can be translated as 'to receive from' or 'to get someone to do something'.
grammars.short_explanation: To receive something or get someone to do something.
grammars.title: ～から もらいます (〜kara moraimasu)

examples.en: He gave me a present.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_私に_くれます_ga_watashi_ni_kuremasu_20250209_彼がプレゼントを私にくれました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼がプレゼントを私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Kare ga purezento wo watashi ni kuremashita.

examples.en: My friend helped me with my homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_私に_くれます_ga_watashi_ni_kuremasu_20250209_友達が宿題を手伝って私にくれました.mp3
examples.jp: 友達が宿題を手伝って私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga shukudai wo tetsudatte watashi ni kuremashita.

examples.en: My mom made me a lunch box.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_私に_くれます_ga_watashi_ni_kuremasu_20250209_お母さんがお弁当を作って私にくれました.mp3
examples.jp: お母さんがお弁当を作って私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ga obentou wo tsukutte watashi ni kuremashita.

examples.en: The teacher gave me advice.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～が_私に_くれます_ga_watashi_ni_kuremasu_20250209_先生がアドバイスを私にくれました.mp3
examples.jp: 先生がアドバイスを私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga adobaisu wo watashi ni kuremashita.

grammars.formation: Person + が + (Thing or Action) + 私に + くれます
grammars.long_explanation: The ～が私にくれます grammar point is used to express that someone gives 'me' something or does something for me. It can be translated as 'someone gives me' or 'someone does something for me' in English. Typically, the giver is marked by が, and the receiver is 私に (to me).
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express that someone gives a gift or favor to 'me'; 'someone gives me'.
grammars.title: ～が 私に くれます (〜ga watashi ni kuremasu)

examples.en: I attended the class, but I still have to do my homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けど～_kedo～_20250209_授業に出たけどまだ宿題をしないといけない.mp3
examples.jp: 授業に出たけど、まだ宿題をしないといけない。
examples.romaji: Jugyou ni deta kedo, mada shukudai wo shinai to ikenai.

examples.en: Yesterday was cold, but today is warm.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けど～_kedo～_20250209_昨日寒かったけど今日は暖かいです.mp3
examples.jp: 昨日寒かったけど、今日は暖かいです。
examples.romaji: Kinou samukatta kedo, kyou wa atatakai desu.

examples.en: He is kind, but a little scary.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けど～_kedo～_20250209_彼は親切だけどちょっと怖い.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は親切だけど、ちょっと怖い。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu da kedo, chotto kowai.

examples.en: This looks delicious, but it is too expensive.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けど～_kedo～_20250209_これはおいしそうだけど高すぎる.mp3
examples.jp: これはおいしそうだけど、高すぎる。
examples.romaji: Kore wa oishisou da kedo, takasugiru.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual + けど / い-adjective + けど / な-adjective + だけど / Noun + だけど
grammars.long_explanation: The ～けど grammar point is used to connect two clauses, often to show a contrast or to introduce a different point of view. It can be translated as 'but', 'however', or 'although' in English. It's more casual than けれど or が.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to connect two clauses; 'but', 'however', 'although'
grammars.title: ～けど、～ (〜kedo、～)

examples.en: Even though it's cold today, I'll go for a walk.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けれど～_keredo～_20250209_今日は寒いけれど散歩に行きます.mp3
examples.jp: 今日は寒いけれど、散歩に行きます。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa samui keredo, sanpo ni ikimasu.

examples.en: He is kind, but a little scary.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けれど～_keredo～_20250209_彼は親切けれど少し怖いです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は親切けれど、少し怖いです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu keredo, sukoshi kowai desu.

examples.en: This room is small, but it's bright.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けれど～_keredo～_20250209_この部屋は狭いけれど明るいです.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋は狭いけれど、明るいです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa semai keredo, akarui desu.

examples.en: She is sick, but she works every day.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～けれど～_keredo～_20250209_彼女は病気だけれど毎日働いています.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は病気だけれど、毎日働いています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa byouki dakeredo, mainichi hataraite imasu.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual + けれど / い-Adjective + けれど / な-Adjective + だけれど / Noun + だけれど
grammars.long_explanation: The ～けれど grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two statements. It can be translated as 'but', 'however', or 'even though' in English. This grammar point is slightly more formal than けど.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
grammars.title: ～けれど、～ (〜keredo、～)

examples.en: This is Mr./Ms. Tanaka.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_こちら～_kochira～_20250209_こちらは田中さんです.mp3
examples.jp: こちらは田中さんです。
examples.romaji: Kochira wa Tanaka-san desu.

examples.en: This restaurant is delicious.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_こちら～_kochira～_20250209_こちらのレストランは美味しいです.mp3
examples.jp: こちらのレストランは美味しいです。
examples.romaji: Kochira no resutoran wa oishii desu.

examples.en: Please come this way.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_こちら～_kochira～_20250209_こちらへどうぞ.mp3
examples.jp: こちらへどうぞ。
examples.romaji: Kochira e douzo.

examples.en: Is this one better, or is that one better?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_こちら～_kochira～_20250209_こちらの方がいいですかそれともあちらの方がいいですか.mp3
examples.jp: こちらの方がいいですか、それともあちらの方がいいですか？
examples.romaji: Kochira no hou ga ii desu ka, sore to mo achira no hou ga ii desu ka?

grammars.formation: こちら / こちら + の + Person/Thing
grammars.long_explanation: The こちら grammar point is used to refer to a person, place, or thing that is closer to the speaker, or to show politeness when referring to someone. It can mean 'this', 'this one', 'this way', or 'here'.
grammars.short_explanation: Refers to a person, place or thing; 'this', 'this one', 'this way', 'here'.
grammars.title: こちら～ (kochira～)

examples.en: There was a phone call just now.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_さっき～_sakki～_20250209_さっき電話がありました.mp3
examples.jp: さっき電話がありました。
examples.romaji: Sakki denwa ga arimashita.

examples.en: I cleaned the room a short while ago.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_さっき～_sakki～_20250209_さっき部屋を掃除しました.mp3
examples.jp: さっき部屋を掃除しました。
examples.romaji: Sakki heya wo souji shimashita.

examples.en: I met him just now.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_さっき～_sakki～_20250209_さっき彼に会いました.mp3
examples.jp: さっき彼に会いました。
examples.romaji: Sakki kare ni aimashita.

examples.en: Did you watch the news a short time ago?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_さっき～_sakki～_20250209_さっきのニュースを見ましたか.mp3
examples.jp: さっきのニュースを見ましたか？
examples.romaji: Sakki no nyuusu wo mimashita ka?

grammars.formation: さっき + verb / さっき + phrase
grammars.long_explanation: The word さっき (sakki) is an adverb used to express that something happened or was done a short time ago or just now. It can be combined with verbs or other phrases to convey that meaning.
grammars.short_explanation: Refers to a short time ago or just now.
grammars.title: さっき～ (sakki～)

examples.en: When my friend arrives, please call me right away.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_すぐに～_sugu_ni～_20250209_友達が来たらすぐに電話をかけてください.mp3
examples.jp: 友達が来たら、すぐに電話をかけてください。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga kitara, sugu ni denwa wo kakete kudasai.

examples.en: Upon hearing that news, I went to the company immediately.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_すぐに～_sugu_ni～_20250209_そのニュースを聞いたらすぐに会社に行きました.mp3
examples.jp: そのニュースを聞いたら、すぐに会社に行きました。
examples.romaji: Sono nyuusu wo kiitara, sugu ni kaisha ni ikimashita.

examples.en: She started crying right away.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_すぐに～_sugu_ni～_20250209_彼女はすぐに泣き出した.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はすぐに泣き出した。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa sugu ni nakidashita.

examples.en: As soon as I entered the classroom, the teacher started the lesson immediately.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_すぐに～_sugu_ni～_20250209_教室に入ると先生はすぐに授業を始めた.mp3
examples.jp: 教室に入ると、先生はすぐに授業を始めた。
examples.romaji: Kyoushitsu ni hairu to, sensei wa sugu ni jugyou wo hajimeta.

grammars.formation: すぐに + Verb/Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The すぐに～ grammar point is used to express an action happening immediately or right away. It often indicates promptness or quickness and can be used with both verbs and adjectives.
grammars.short_explanation: Immediately or right away; used to express promptness or quickness.
grammars.title: すぐに～ (sugu ni～)

examples.en: He doesn't talk at all.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_ぜんぜん～_zenzen～_20250209_彼はぜんぜん話さない.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はぜんぜん話さない。
examples.romaji: Kare wa zenzen hanasanai.

examples.en: This room is not dark at all.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_ぜんぜん～_zenzen～_20250209_この部屋はぜんぜん暗くない.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋はぜんぜん暗くない。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa zenzen kurakunai.

examples.en: She is not tired at all.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_ぜんぜん～_zenzen～_20250209_彼女はぜんぜん疲れていない.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はぜんぜん疲れていない。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa zenzen tsukarete inai.

examples.en: That movie was not interesting at all.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_ぜんぜん～_zenzen～_20250209_その映画はぜんぜん面白くなかった.mp3
examples.jp: その映画はぜんぜん面白くなかった。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa zenzen omoshirokunakatta.

grammars.formation: ぜんぜん + [Negative verb/adjective]
grammars.long_explanation: The ぜんぜん grammar point is used to emphasize a negative statement and can be translated as 'not at all' or 'completely (in negative sense)'. It is commonly used with negative verbs or negative forms of adjectives, placed before the negative part.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'not at all' or 'completely' in negative sentences.
grammars.title: ぜんぜん～ (zenzen～)

examples.en: I woke up in the morning and then did my homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そして～_soshite～_20250209_朝起きてそして宿題をしました.mp3
examples.jp: 朝起きて、そして宿題をしました。
examples.romaji: Asa okite, soshite shukudai wo shimashita.

examples.en: I drank coffee and then read the newspaper.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そして～_soshite～_20250209_コーヒーを飲んでそして新聞を読みました.mp3
examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、そして新聞を読みました。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo nonde, soshite shinbun wo yomimashita.

examples.en: I left my house and then went to the station.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そして～_soshite～_20250209_家を出発しましたそして駅へ行きました.mp3
examples.jp: 家を出発しました。そして、駅へ行きました。
examples.romaji: Ie wo shuppatsu shimashita. Soshite, eki e ikimashita.

examples.en: He played games and then watched TV.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そして～_soshite～_20250209_彼はゲームをしたそしてテレビを見ました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はゲームをした。そして、テレビを見ました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa geemu wo shita. Soshite, terebi wo mimashita.

grammars.formation: Sentence 1 + そして + Sentence 2
grammars.long_explanation: The そして grammar point is used to connect two sentences or ideas, expressing a sequence of events or actions. It is commonly translated to 'and then' or simply 'and' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'and then', 'and'.
grammars.title: そして、～ (soshite、～)

examples.en: How is that restaurant over there?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そちら～_sochira～_20250209_そちらのレストランはどうですか.mp3
examples.jp: そちらのレストランはどうですか？
examples.romaji: Sochira no resutoran wa dou desu ka?

examples.en: Could you tell me the name of that person over there?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そちら～_sochira～_20250209_そちらの方お名前を教えていただけますか.mp3
examples.jp: そちらの方、お名前を教えていただけますか？
examples.romaji: Sochira no kata, onamae o oshiete itadakemasu ka?

examples.en: There is a station on the way to that direction.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そちら～_sochira～_20250209_そちらに行く途中で駅があります.mp3
examples.jp: そちらに行く途中で駅があります。
examples.romaji: Sochira ni iku tochuu de eki ga arimasu.

examples.en: That bag over there looks similar to mine.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_そちら～_sochira～_20250209_そちらのかばん私のと似ていますね.mp3
examples.jp: そちらのかばん、私のと似ていますね。
examples.romaji: Sochira no kaban, watashi no to niteimasu ne.

grammars.formation: そちら [alone] / そちら + の + Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The そちら grammar point is used to refer to a direction or a person that is moderate distance from both the speaker and listener, often closer to the listener. It can be translated as 'that way', 'that person', or 'that side'. This is distinct from あちら, used for things far from both speaker and listener.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates a direction or person in moderate distance; 'that way', 'that person'.
grammars.title: そちら～ (sochira～)

examples.en: I drank coffee, and then I left the house.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_それから～_sorekara～_20250209_コーヒーを飲んでそれから家を出ました.mp3
examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、それから家を出ました。
examples.romaji: Koohii o nonde, sorekara ie o demashita.

examples.en: I went shopping, and then I went to watch a movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_それから～_sorekara～_20250209_買い物をしてそれから映画を見に行きました.mp3
examples.jp: 買い物をして、それから映画を見に行きました。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o shite, sorekara eiga o mini ikimashita.

examples.en: She studied, and then she went to sleep.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_それから～_sorekara～_20250209_彼女は勉強をしてそれから寝ました.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は勉強をして、それから寝ました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa benkyou o shite, sorekara nemashita.

examples.en: I went to the party, and then I talked with my friends.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_それから～_sorekara～_20250209_パーティーに行ってそれから友達と話しました.mp3
examples.jp: パーティーに行って、それから友達と話しました。
examples.romaji: Paatii ni itte, sorekara tomodachi to hanashimashita.

grammars.formation: Clause 1 + それから + Clause 2
grammars.long_explanation: The それから grammar point is used to describe the sequence of events or actions, indicating that one action or event takes place after another. It can be translated as 'after that', 'and then', or 'then' in English. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns but should be placed between two clauses.
grammars.short_explanation: Meaning 'after that', 'and then' or 'then', indicating sequence of events.
grammars.title: それから、～ (sorekara、～)

examples.en: Approximately 100 people attended the party.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だいたい_daitai_20250209_だいたい１００人がパーティーに参加しました.mp3
examples.jp: だいたい１００人がパーティーに参加しました。
examples.romaji: Daitai hyaku-nin ga paatii ni sanka shimashita.

examples.en: She finishes that work in roughly two hours.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だいたい_daitai_20250209_彼女はだいたい２時間でその仕事を終えます.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はだいたい２時間でその仕事を終えます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa daitai ni-jikan de sono shigoto o oemasu.

examples.en: About 80% of the students passed the exam.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だいたい_daitai_20250209_だいたい８０％の生徒が試験に合格しました.mp3
examples.jp: だいたい８０％の生徒が試験に合格しました。
examples.romaji: Daitai hachijuu-paasento no seito ga shiken ni goukaku shimashita.

examples.en: Today is almost 30 degrees hot.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だいたい_daitai_20250209_今日はだいたい３０度の暑さです.mp3
examples.jp: 今日はだいたい３０度の暑さです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa daitai sanjuu-do no atsusa desu.

grammars.formation: だいたい + Number/Amount/Percentage
grammars.long_explanation: The だいたい〜 (daitai〜) grammar point is used to express a rough estimate or generalization, meaning 'roughly', 'approximately', or 'almost' in English. It can be used before numbers, amounts, or percentages to show that the value is not exact.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'roughly', 'approximately', or 'almost'.
grammars.title: だいたい〜 (daitai〜)

examples.en: I usually wake up at 8 o'clock in the morning.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_たいてい～_taitei～_20250209_たいてい朝８時に起きます.mp3
examples.jp: たいてい朝８時に起きます。
examples.romaji: Taitei asa hachi-ji ni okimasu.

examples.en: He is usually late.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_たいてい～_taitei～_20250209_彼はたいてい遅刻します.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はたいてい遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kare wa taitei chikoku shimasu.

examples.en: The items at this store are usually cheap.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_たいてい～_taitei～_20250209_この店の商品はたいてい安いです.mp3
examples.jp: この店の商品はたいてい安いです。
examples.romaji: Kono mise no shouhin wa taitei yasui desu.

examples.en: Most people like that movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_たいてい～_taitei～_20250209_たいていの人はその映画が好きです.mp3
examples.jp: たいていの人はその映画が好きです。
examples.romaji: Taitei no hito wa sono eiga ga suki desu.

grammars.formation: たいてい + Verb/い-Adjective/な-Adjective/Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The たいてい grammar point is used to describe a situation that occurs frequently or under normal circumstances. It can be translated as 'usually', 'mostly', or 'generally' in English. It is often used with verbs, but can also be used with adjectives and nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: Used for expressing 'usually', 'mostly', or 'generally'.
grammars.title: たいてい～ (taitei～)

examples.en: Because it's raining, let's bring an umbrella.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だから～_dakara～_20250209_雨だから傘を持って行きましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 雨だから、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Ame dakara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.

examples.en: Because this cake is famous, everyone wants to eat it.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だから～_dakara～_20250209_このケーキは有名だからみんなが食べたいです.mp3
examples.jp: このケーキは有名だから、みんなが食べたいです。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa yuumei dakara, minna ga tabetai desu.

examples.en: Because he is sick, he cannot go to school.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だから～_dakara～_20250209_彼は病気だから学校に行けません.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は病気だから、学校に行けません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki dakara, gakkou ni ikemasen.

examples.en: Because she is a student, there is a discount at this restaurant.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だから～_dakara～_20250209_彼女は学生だからこのレストランで割引があります.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は学生だから、このレストランで割引があります。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei dakara, kono resutoran de waribiki ga arimasu.

grammars.formation: Noun + だから / な-Adjective + だから
grammars.long_explanation: The だから grammar point is used to connect two sentences and express a reason or cause for the second sentence. It is typically used with nouns or な-adjectives, and can be translated as 'because', 'so', or 'therefore' in English. For verbs/い-adjectives, the form is usually ～から (not だから).
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses a reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
grammars.title: だから、～ (dakara、～)

examples.en: On holidays, I do things like watch movies and hang out with friends.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～たり～たり_します_tari_tari_shimasu_20250209_休日には映画を見たり友達と遊んだりします.mp3
examples.jp: 休日には、映画を見たり、友達と遊んだりします。
examples.romaji: Kyuujitsu ni wa, eiga wo mitari, tomodachi to asondari shimasu.

examples.en: He sings, dances, plays the piano, among other things.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～たり～たり_します_tari_tari_shimasu_20250209_彼は歌ったり踊ったりピアノを弾いたりします.mp3
examples.jp: 彼は歌ったり、踊ったり、ピアノを弾いたりします。
examples.romaji: Kare wa utattari, odottari, piano wo hikitari shimasu.

examples.en: At this restaurant, you can eat sushi, sashimi, and so on.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～たり～たり_します_tari_tari_shimasu_20250209_このレストランでは寿司を食べたり刺身を食べたりします.mp3
examples.jp: このレストランでは、寿司を食べたり、刺身を食べたりします。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran de wa, sushi wo tabetari, sashimi wo tabetari shimasu.

examples.en: Every morning, she does things like jogging and yoga.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～たり～たり_します_tari_tari_shimasu_20250209_彼女は毎朝ジョギングしたりヨガをしたりします.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女は毎朝、ジョギングしたり、ヨガをしたりします。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa maiasa, joggingu shitari, yoga wo shitari shimasu.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual-past + たり + Verb-casual-past + たり + します
grammars.long_explanation: The ～たり、～たり します grammar point is used to list multiple actions or states without fully enumerating them. It can imply that there are more items in the list and can be translated as 'do things like', 'and', 'among other things', or 'and so on' in English. It is formed by attaching たり to the casual past tense of the verb, followed by します.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to list multiple actions or states; 'do things like', 'and'.
grammars.title: ～たり、～たり します (〜tari, 〜tari shimasu)

examples.en: Who bought that book?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれ～_dare～_20250209_だれがその本を買いましたか.mp3
examples.jp: だれがその本を買いましたか。
examples.romaji: Dare ga sono hon o kaimashita ka.

examples.en: Whom are you waiting for?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれ～_dare～_20250209_だれを待っていますか.mp3
examples.jp: だれを待っていますか。
examples.romaji: Dare o matteimasu ka.

examples.en: Who ate that apple?

examples.romaji: Dare ga sono ringo o tabemashita ka.

examples.romaji: Dare ga kagi o motteimasu ka.

grammars.formation: だれ + appropriate particle (が, は or を)
grammars.long_explanation: The だれ〜 grammar point is used to ask about the identity of someone in a sentence. It can be translated as 'who' or 'whom' in English. It is often used with the particle が, は, or を, but can also be combined with other particles depending on the context.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking 'who' in a sentence, used to inquire about someone's identity or to clarify who is being referred to.
grammars.title: だれ～ (dare～)

examples.en: Someone knocked on the door.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれか_dareka_20250209_だれかがドアをノックしました.mp3

examples.romaji: Dareka ga doa wo nokku shimashita.

examples.en: Someone stole my umbrella.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれか_dareka_20250209_だれかが私の傘を盗みました.mp3
examples.jp: だれかが私の傘を盗みました。
examples.romaji: Dareka ga watashi no kasa wo nusumimashita.

examples.en: Someone, please help.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれか_dareka_20250209_だれか助けてください.mp3
examples.jp: だれか助けてください。
examples.romaji: Dareka tasukete kudasai.

examples.en: Because of someone, the electricity went out.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれか_dareka_20250209_だれかのせいで電気がきれました.mp3
examples.jp: だれかのせいで、電気がきれました。
examples.romaji: Dareka no sei de, denki ga kiremashita.

grammars.formation: だれか + Verb, だれか + Adjective, だれか + Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point だれか〜 is used to suggest that something is done by, possessed by, or related to 'someone', usually when the actual person is unidentified or not important. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates 'someone' or something done or possessed by 'someone'.
grammars.title: だれか〜 (dareka〜)

examples.en: Anyone can play this game.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれでも～_dare_demo～_20250209_だれでもこのゲームができます.mp3
examples.jp: だれでもこのゲームができます。
examples.romaji: Dare demo kono geemu ga dekimasu.

examples.en: Everyone gets tired sometimes.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれでも～_dare_demo～_20250209_だれでも疲れることがあります.mp3
examples.jp: だれでも疲れることがあります。
examples.romaji: Dare demo tsukareru koto ga arimasu.

examples.en: Anyone can participate in this event for free.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれでも～_dare_demo～_20250209_だれでも無料でこのイベントに参加できます.mp3
examples.jp: だれでも無料でこのイベントに参加できます。
examples.romaji: Dare demo muryou de kono ibento ni sanka dekimasu.

examples.en: No matter who you are, you can enjoy the sightseeing spots in this town.

examples.romaji: Dare demo kono machi no kankou supotto wo tanoshimu koto ga dekimasu.

grammars.formation: だれでも + Verb/Adjective/Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point だれでも is used to emphasize that something applies to everyone or anyone, regardless of who they are. It can be translated as 'anyone', 'everyone', or 'no matter who' in English. It is used in sentences to show that a certain situation, characteristic, or condition applies to all people.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'anyone' or 'everyone'; 'no matter who'.
grammars.title: だれでも～ (dare demo～)

examples.en: Nobody knows.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ないです_dare_mo__nai_desu_20250209_だれも知らないです.mp3
examples.jp: だれも知らないです。
examples.romaji: Daremo shiranai desu.

examples.en: Nobody is coming.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ないです_dare_mo__nai_desu_20250209_だれも来ないです.mp3
examples.jp: だれも来ないです。
examples.romaji: Daremo konai desu.

examples.en: She doesn't like anyone.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ないです_dare_mo__nai_desu_20250209_彼女はだれも好きじゃないです.mp3
examples.jp: 彼女はだれも好きじゃないです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa daremo suki ja nai desu.

examples.en: There is nobody here.

examples.jp: ここにはだれもいないです。
examples.romaji: Koko ni wa daremo inai desu.

grammars.formation: だれも + Verb-negative form (ないです), だれも + い-Adjective-negative form (ないです), だれも + な-Adjective-negative form (じゃないです)
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point だれも～ないです is used to express the idea of 'nobody' or 'no one' in a negative sentence. だれも is followed by the negative form of a verb or adjective, often using the polite ないです form.
grammars.short_explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in a negative sentence.
grammars.title: だれも～ないです (dare mo ~ nai desu)

examples.en: No one knows the secret.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ません_daremo_masen_20250209_だれも秘密を知りません.mp3
examples.jp: だれも秘密を知りません。
examples.romaji: Daremo himitsu wo shirimasen.

examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ません_daremo_masen_20250209_だれもその質問に答えませんでした.mp3
examples.jp: だれもその質問に答えませんでした。
examples.romaji: Daremo sono shitsumon ni kotaemasen deshita.

examples.en: Nobody will help him.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ません_daremo_masen_20250209_だれも彼を助けてあげません.mp3
examples.jp: だれも彼を助けてあげません。
examples.romaji: Daremo kare wo tasukete agemasen.

examples.en: No one wants to watch that movie.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_だれも～ません_daremo_masen_20250209_だれもその映画を見たがりません.mp3

examples.romaji: Daremo sono eiga wo mitagarimasen.

grammars.formation: だれも + Verb-negative (ません)
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point だれも is used in combination with a negative form of the verb, usually ません, to express the idea of 'nobody' or 'no one' doing something. It is used with questions or statements and can be translated as 'nobody' or 'no one' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in negative sentences.
grammars.title: だれも～ません (daremo ~masen)

examples.en: It's raining, so what will you do?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どう_しますか_～dou_shimasu_ka_20250209_雨が降っているのでどうしますか.mp3
examples.jp: 雨が降っているので、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Ame ga futte iru node, dou shimasu ka?

examples.en: What are you going to do about this issue?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どう_しますか_～dou_shimasu_ka_20250209_この問題についてどうしますか.mp3
examples.jp: この問題について、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Kono mondai ni tsuite, dou shimasu ka?

examples.en: If he doesn't come, what will you do?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どう_しますか_～dou_shimasu_ka_20250209_彼が来なかったらどうしますか.mp3
examples.jp: 彼が来なかったら、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Kare ga konakattara, dou shimasu ka?

examples.en: What will you do when choosing your career path?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どう_しますか_～dou_shimasu_ka_20250209_進路を決める時どうしますか.mp3
examples.jp: 進路を決める時、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Shinro wo kimeru toki, dou shimasu ka?

grammars.formation: Situation + どうしますか
grammars.long_explanation: The ～どうしますか grammar point is used to ask for someone's opinion, decision, or course of action in a specific situation. It can be translated as 'what will you do?' or 'how will you handle it?' in English. This grammar point is formed by attaching どうしますか to the end of a sentence.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking for someone's opinion or decision; 'what will you do?', 'how will you handle it?'.
grammars.title: ～どう しますか。 (～dou shimasu ka.)

examples.en: How about this movie? / What do you think of this movie?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どうですか_dou_desu_ka_20250209_この映画はどうですか.mp3
examples.jp: この映画はどうですか？
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa dou desu ka?

examples.en: How about eating sushi for dinner?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どうですか_dou_desu_ka_20250209_晩ご飯に寿司を食べるのはどうですか.mp3
examples.jp: 晩ご飯に寿司を食べるのはどうですか？
examples.romaji: Bangohan ni sushi wo taberu no wa dou desu ka?

examples.en: I think this room is spacious, what do you think?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どうですか_dou_desu_ka_20250209_この部屋は広いと思いますがどうですか.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋は広いと思いますが、どうですか？
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hiroi to omoimasu ga, dou desu ka?

examples.en: The new company's requirements are strict, aren't they? Suzuki-san, how about changing jobs if that's the case?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どうですか_dou_desu_ka_20250209_新しい会社の要件が厳しいですね鈴木さん転職するならどうですか.mp3
examples.jp: 新しい会社の要件が厳しいですね。鈴木さん、転職するならどうですか？
examples.romaji: Atarashii kaisha no youken ga kibishii desu ne. Suzuki-san, tenshoku suru nara dou desu ka?

grammars.formation: Noun + は/が + どうですか / Verb-casual + の + どうですか / い-Adjective + どうですか / な-Adjective + な + どうですか
grammars.long_explanation: The ～どうですか grammar point is used to ask for someone's opinion or suggestion on something. It can be translated as 'how about' or 'what do you think of' in English. This expression is neither casual nor super-formal, and can be used in various situations.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking for opinions or suggestions; 'how about', 'what do you think of'.
grammars.title: ～どうですか。 (〜dou desu ka.)

examples.en: How do you make sushi?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どうやって～_douyatte～_20250209_どうやってお寿司を作りますか.mp3
examples.jp: どうやってお寿司を作りますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte o-sushi wo tsukurimasu ka?

examples.en: How did you study Japanese?

examples.jp: どうやって日本語を勉強しましたか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte nihongo wo benkyou shimashita ka?

examples.en: How do you solve this problem?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どうやって～_douyatte～_20250209_どうやってこの問題を解決しますか.mp3
examples.jp: どうやってこの問題を解決しますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte kono mondai wo kaiketsu shimasu ka?

examples.en: How do you go to the station?

examples.jp: どうやって駅に行きますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte eki ni ikimasu ka?

grammars.formation: どうやって + Verb-casual
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point どうやって is used to ask how something is done or how to do something, and is translated as 'how' in English. It is often used in combination with verbs to inquire about the method or process someone goes through to complete a task or action.
grammars.short_explanation: Ask 'how' something is done or how to do something.
grammars.title: どうやって～ (douyatte～)

examples.en: How do you say 'thank you' in English?

examples.jp: 「すみません」はフランス語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: 「Sumimasen」wa furansugo de dou iimasu ka.

examples.en: How do you say that expression in Spanish?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～どう_言いますか_dou_iimasu_ka_20250209_その表現をスペイン語でどう言いますか.mp3
examples.jp: その表現をスペイン語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: Sono hyougen wo supeingo de dou iimasu ka.

grammars.formation: Word/Phrase + は [language]でどう言いますか / Word/Phrase + をどう言いますか
grammars.long_explanation: The ～どう言いますか grammar point is used to ask someone how to express something in a particular language or the appropriate way to say it. It can be translated as 'how do you say' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking for the way to say something; 'how do you say'.
grammars.title: ～どう 言いますか。 (〜dou iimasu ka.)

examples.en: When playing in the park, let's wear a hat.

examples.romaji: Kono ringo ga akai toki, tabegoro desu.

examples.romaji: Watashi ga benkyou suru toki, kazoku wa shizuka ni shite kuremasu.

examples.en: When I was a child, I often went to play at my grandmother's house.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～とき_toki_20250209_子供のときよくおばあちゃんの家に遊びに行きました.mp3

examples.romaji: Kodomo no toki, yoku obaachan no ie ni asobi ni ikimashita.

grammars.formation: Verb-casual + とき / い-Adjective + とき / な-Adjective + なとき / Noun + のとき
grammars.long_explanation: The ～とき grammar point is used to express the time when something happens or happened. It can be translated as 'when' or 'at the time' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses the time when something happens, 'when', 'at the time'.
grammars.title: ～とき (〜toki)

examples.jp: ときどき雨が降るので、傘を持って行ったほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Tokidoki ame ga furu node, kasa o motte itta hou ga ii desu.

examples.en: I shop at this store now and then.

examples.romaji: Watashi wa tokidoki kono mise de kaimono o shimasu.

examples.en: She is sometimes late.

examples.jp: 彼女はときどき遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa tokidoki chikoku shimasu.

grammars.formation: ときどき + Verb/Adjective/Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point ときどき is an adverb used to describe an event or action that occurs occasionally or at irregular intervals. It can be translated as 'sometimes', 'occasionally', or 'now and then' in English. It is often used to indicate that the speaker cannot predict the exact time when a certain event occurs.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to indicate the frequency of an event; 'sometimes', 'occasionally', 'now and then'.
grammars.title: ときどき～ (tokidoki～)

examples.en: Where is the station?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どこ～_doko～_20250209_駅はどこですか.mp3
examples.jp: 駅はどこですか？
examples.romaji: Eki wa doko desu ka?

examples.romaji: Doko e ikitai desu ka?

grammars.long_explanation: The どこ～ grammar point is used to express 'where', primarily for asking about locations or places. It is often combined with question words such as どこへ (doko e), どこで (doko de), and どこに (doko ni) to ask about destinations, locations of actions, and existence, respectively.
grammars.short_explanation: Express 'where', used with question words for asking about locations.
grammars.title: どこ～ (doko～)

examples.romaji: Dokoka de saifu wo nakushimashita.

examples.en: I want to go somewhere today.

examples.romaji: Kyou wa dokoka ni ikitai desu.

examples.en: Is there a cheap restaurant somewhere?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どこか～_dokoka～_20250209_どこか安いレストランがありますか.mp3
examples.jp: どこか安いレストランがありますか？
examples.romaji: Dokoka yasui resutoran ga arimasu ka?

examples.en: I want to study in a quiet place somewhere.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どこか～_dokoka～_20250209_どこか静かな場所で勉強したい.mp3
examples.jp: どこか静かな場所で勉強したい。
examples.romaji: Dokoka shizuka na basho de benkyou shitai.

grammars.formation: どこか + (Particle, if needed) + Verb/Noun/Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point どこか is used when the speaker wants to express that something is happening or located 'somewhere', but the exact location is either unknown or uncertain. It can be used by itself or combined with other words.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'somewhere', used when the specific location is unknown or uncertain.
grammars.title: どこか～ (dokoka～)

examples.en: You can study anywhere you like.

examples.jp: どこでも好きな場所で勉強できます。
examples.romaji: Dokodemo sukina basho de benkyou dekimasu.

examples.en: This laptop is convenient, so you can use the internet anywhere.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どこでも～_dokodemo～_20250209_このノートパソコンは便利なのでどこでもインターネットが使えます.mp3
examples.jp: このノートパソコンは便利なので、どこでもインターネットが使えます。
examples.romaji: Kono nootopasokon wa benri nano de, dokodemo intaanetto ga tsukaemasu.

examples.en: He can sleep anywhere.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_どこでも～_dokodemo～_20250209_彼はどこでも寝ることができます.mp3
examples.jp: 彼はどこでも寝ることができます。

grammars.long_explanation: The なにか grammar point is used to express the idea of 'something' or 'some kind of' in Japanese. It is often used when the speaker is unsure or not specific about the details of the noun being referred to. なにか is used before the noun it modifies.
grammars.short_explanation: Indicates 'something' or 'some kind of'.
grammars.title: なにか～ (nanika～)

examples.en: He didn't say anything.

examples.jp: 彼はなにも言わなかったです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa nani mo iwanakatta desu.

examples.en: I don't eat anything.

examples.romaji: Watashi wa nani mo tabenai desu.

examples.en: She doesn't have anything.

examples.romaji: Kanojo wa nani mo motte inai desu.

examples.en: There is nothing in this box.

examples.jp: この箱にはなにも入っていないです。
examples.romaji: Kono hako ni wa nani mo haitte inai desu.

grammars.formation: なにも + Verb-negative
grammars.long_explanation: The なにも～ないです grammar point is used in negative sentences to express the idea of 'not any', 'not at all', 'nothing', or 'none'. It is commonly used with verbs in the negative form.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'not any' or 'nothing' in a negative sentence.
grammars.title: なにも～ないです (nani mo~nai desu)

examples.en: I didn't eat anything yesterday.

examples.romaji: Kinou wa nanimo tabemasen deshita.

examples.jp: 彼はなにも話しません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa nanimo hanashimasen.

examples.en: I cannot see anything in this room.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なにも～ません_nanimomasen_20250209_この部屋ではなにも見えません.mp3
examples.jp: この部屋ではなにも見えません。
examples.romaji: Kono heya de wa nanimo miemasen.

examples.en: She didn't buy anything.

examples.jp: 彼女はなにも買いませんでした。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa nanimo kaimasen deshita.

grammars.formation: なにも + Verb-ます form + ません
grammars.long_explanation: The grammar point なにも～ません is used to express the idea of 'not anything' or 'nothing' in negative sentences. It is placed before the verb in its negative form (～ません).
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'not anything', 'nothing'.
grammars.title: なにも～ません (nanimo~masen)

examples.en: How old are you?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なん～_nan_20250209_あなたはなん歳ですか.mp3
examples.jp: あなたはなん歳ですか？
examples.romaji: Anata wa nan-sai desu ka?

examples.romaji: Kore wa nan desu ka?

examples.en: What is the name of that restaurant?

examples.romaji: Ano resutoran wa nan to iu namae desu ka?

grammars.formation: なん + Counter / なん + Verb / なん + Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The なん～ grammar point is used to form interrogative questions and emphasize the question word for 'what' or 'how'. It is an abbreviation of '何' meaning 'what'. Its usage can vary depending on whether it is used with a counter, verb, or adjective.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to form interrogative questions and emphasize the question word for 'what', 'how'.
grammars.title: なん～ (nan~)

examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんで～_nande～_20250209_なんで遅れたの.mp3
examples.jp: なんで遅れたの？
examples.romaji: Nande okureta no?

examples.en: Why is this room so dirty?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんで～_nande～_20250209_なんでこの部屋はこんなに汚いの.mp3
examples.jp: なんでこの部屋はこんなに汚いの？
examples.romaji: Nande kono heya wa konna ni kitanai no?

examples.en: Why is she angry?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんで～_nande～_20250209_なんで彼女は怒っているの.mp3
examples.jp: なんで彼女は怒っているの？
examples.romaji: Nande kanojo wa okotte iru no?

examples.en: Why is today a holiday?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんで～_nande～_20250209_なんで今日は休みなの.mp3
examples.jp: なんで今日は休みなの？
examples.romaji: Nande kyou wa yasumi na no?

grammars.formation: なんで + [phrase or sentence]
grammars.long_explanation: The なんで grammar point is used to ask the reason or cause behind something. It can be translated as 'why' or 'how come' in English. It is a casual way of asking for an explanation, and it can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking the reason or cause; 'why', 'how come'.
grammars.title: なんで～ (nande～)

examples.en: I can eat anything, so it's okay to order whatever you want.

examples.romaji: Nandemo taberareru kara, nani wo tanondemo daijoubu desu.

examples.en: If you're okay with anything, I recommend this book.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんでも～_nandemo～_20250209_なんでもよければこの本をおすすめします.mp3
examples.jp: なんでもよければ、この本をおすすめします。
examples.romaji: Nandemo yokereba, kono hon wo osusume shimasu.

examples.en: We are looking for a staff member who can do anything.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんでも～_nandemo～_20250209_なんでもできるスタッフを探しています.mp3
examples.jp: なんでもできるスタッフを探しています。
examples.romaji: Nandemo dekiru sutaffu wo sagashiteimasu.

examples.en: In this cafeteria, any dish served is delicious and inexpensive.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_なんでも～_nandemo～_20250209_この食堂ではなんでも美味しくて安い料理が出されます.mp3
examples.jp: この食堂では、なんでも美味しくて安い料理が出されます。
examples.romaji: Kono shokudou de wa, nandemo oishikute yasui ryouri ga dasaremasu.

grammars.formation: なんでも + Verb / なんでも + Adjective / なんでも + Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The なんでも grammar point is used to express the concept of 'any', 'anything', or 'anyone' in Japanese. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns. It is often used in the meaning of 'no matter what' or 'regardless of'.
grammars.short_explanation: Means 'any', 'anything', 'anyone'.
grammars.title: なんでも～ (nandemo～)

examples.en: How do you say this flower?

examples.jp: この花はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Kono hana wa nan to iimasu ka.

examples.en: What do you call this dish?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～なんと_言いますか_nan_to_iimasu_ka_20250209_この料理はなんと言いますか.mp3
examples.jp: この料理はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa nan to iimasu ka.

examples.en: How do you say this in Japanese?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～なんと_言いますか_nan_to_iimasu_ka_20250209_日本でこれはなんと言いますか.mp3
examples.jp: 日本でこれはなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Nihon de kore wa nan to iimasu ka.

examples.en: What is the name of that movie?
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～なんと_言いますか_nan_to_iimasu_ka_20250209_その映画の名前はなんと言いますか.mp3
examples.jp: その映画の名前はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga no namae wa nan to iimasu ka.

grammars.formation: Noun + は/が + なんと言いますか
grammars.long_explanation: The ～なんと言いますか grammar point is used to ask how something is called, expressed, or referred to in a polite manner. It can be translated as 'how do you say' or 'what do you call' in English. The formation is used with a noun or a topic where you would like to know the proper expression or name for something.
grammars.short_explanation: Asking how something is called or referred to; 'how do you say'
grammars.title: ～なんと 言いますか。 (〜nan to iimasu ka.)

examples.en: I gave a book to my friend.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～に_あげます__ni_agemasu_20250209_私は友達に本をあげました.mp3
examples.jp: 私は友達に本をあげました。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa tomodachi ni hon wo agemashita.

examples.en: Let's give him a present.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～に_あげます__ni_agemasu_20250209_彼にプレゼントをあげましょう.mp3
examples.jp: 彼にプレゼントをあげましょう。
examples.romaji: Kare ni purezento wo agemashou.

examples.romaji: Okaasan ni chokoreeto wo agetai desu.

grammars.formation: Receiver + に + Object + を + あげます
grammars.long_explanation: The ～に あげます grammar point is used when the speaker offers or gives something to someone. It emphasizes that the action is performed for the benefit of the receiver. The formation involves using the particle 'に' after the person receiving the item, followed by the verb あげます.
grammars.short_explanation: Used to express giving something to someone; 'give', 'offer'.
grammars.title: ～に あげます (〜 ni agemasu)

examples.en: I received a gift from my friend.

examples.jp: 友達にプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni purezento wo moraimashita.

examples.jp: 先生にアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni adobaisu wo moraimashita.

examples.romaji: Obaasan ni tegami wo kaite moraimashita.

examples.en: I got help from my younger brother with my homework.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～に_もらいます_ni_moraimasu_20250209_弟に宿題を手伝ってもらいました.mp3

examples.romaji: Otouto ni shukudai wo tetsudatte moraimashita.

grammars.formation: Giver + に + Verb-te form + もらいます / Giver + に + Object + を + もらいます
grammars.long_explanation: The ～に もらいます grammar point is used to express receiving something or some action from someone. It can be translated as 'to get' or 'to receive' in English. The formation involves placing に after the giver and もらいます to show the act of receiving.
grammars.short_explanation: To receive something or some action from someone; 'to get', 'to receive'.
grammars.title: ～に もらいます (〜ni moraimasu)

examples.en: This is my bag.
examples.grammar_audio: /audio/japanese/grammar/s_～の_no_20250209_これは私の鞄です.mp3
examples.jp: これは私の鞄です。
examples.romaji: Kore wa watashi no kaban desu.

examples.en: She has a red bag.

grammars.short_explanation: Express possession, apposition, or description using 'of' or ''s'.
grammars.title: ～の (〜no)

grammars.formation: Noun + はたいへんです
grammars.long_explanation: The ～はたいへんです grammar point is used to express that something is difficult or tough to do, handle, or face. It can be translated as 'is difficult' or 'is tough' in English. The formation is used with a noun followed by はたいへんです.
grammars.short_explanation: Express that something is difficult or tough.
grammars.title: ～はたいへんです (〜wa taihen desu)

grammars.short_explanation: Used to express 'almost', 'nearly', or 'most'.
grammars.title: ほとんど〜 (hotondo〜)

examples.romaji: Kyou no tenki wa maa maa desu ne.

grammars.short_explanation: Expresses something as 'so-so', 'not bad', or 'average'.
grammars.title: まあまあ～ (maa maa～)

grammars.long_explanation: The まだ〜 grammar point is used to express that something has not yet occurred or is still in progress. It can be translated as 'still' or 'not yet' in English. grammars.short_explanation: Indicates something has not yet happened or is still happening; 'still', 'not yet'.

grammars.formation: まだ + Verb-negative + です
grammars.long_explanation: The まだ〜ないです grammar point is used to indicate that a certain action or event has not yet happened or been completed. It is used with the negative form of a verb (casual negative + です) and can be translated as 'not yet', 'still', or 'haven't' in English.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet.
grammars.title: まだ〜ないです (mada 〜 nai desu)

grammars.formation: まだ + Verb-ます form (negative)
grammars.long_explanation: The まだ～ません grammar point is used to express that something has not happened or been done yet in a polite register. It is used with the negative ます-form of a verb (～ません). まだ is placed before the verb phrase.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet (polite form).
grammars.title: まだ～ません (mada ~masen)

grammars.formation: もう + Verb / もう + Adjective / もう + Noun
grammars.long_explanation: The もう grammar point is used to express the idea of 'already', 'anymore', or 'soon' in English. It indicates that something has already happened, won't happen anymore, or will happen soon. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns depending on context.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'already', 'anymore', or 'soon'.
grammars.title: もう～ (mou～)

grammars.formation: もうすぐ + Verb (~ます form or 〜る form)
grammars.long_explanation: The もうすぐ grammar point is used to express that an action or event is going to happen soon or is almost happening. It can be translated as 'soon', 'in a short while', or 'almost' in English. もうすぐ is usually followed by a verb or a noun indicating an event.
grammars.short_explanation: Express an action or event happening soon: 'soon', 'in a short while', 'almost'.
grammars.title: もうすぐ〜 (mou sugu~)

grammars.formation: もっと + Verb / い-Adjective / な-Adjective
grammars.long_explanation: The もっと〜 grammar point is used to emphasize the desire or need for something to be 'more' or 'even more' in terms of quantity, frequency, or degree. It is often translated as 'more' or 'even more' in English. もっと can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, or な-adjectives.
grammars.short_explanation: Expresses 'more' or 'even more' when describing a quantity, frequency, or degree.
grammars.title: もっと〜 (motto〜)

grammars.short_explanation: Often used to express 'doing something well' or 'often'.
grammars.title: よく～ (yoku ~)

grammars.formation: Place + に + Object/Thing + が + あります
grammars.long_explanation: The ～（場所）に～があります grammar point is used to express the existence or presence of something in a specific location. In this structure, the place is followed by 'に', then the object, plus が, and finally あります (to exist / there is).
grammars.short_explanation: Express the existence or presence of something in a place.
grammars.title: ～（場所）に～があります (〜basho ni 〜 ga arimasu)
